sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第289卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Roll 289
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 289

sentences.zh: 【後漢紀四】上章閹茂，一年。

translations.literal: [Later Han Records 4] From Shangzhang Yanmao; one year in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Han Records 4] From Shangzhang Yanmao—one year in all.

sentences.zh: 隱皇帝下乾祐三年（

translations.literal: Under the Hidden Emperor, third year of Qianyou (
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yin, third year of Qianyou (

sentences.zh: 庚戌，公元九五零年）

translations.literal: gengxu, the year 950 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengxu, 950 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁未，加鳳翔節度使趙暉兼侍中。

translations.literal: In spring, first month, on dingwei, Zhao Hui, military governor of Fengxiang, was additionally appointed Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingwei, Zhao Hui, military governor of Fengxiang, was given the additional title of Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 密州刺史王萬敢請益兵以攻唐。

translations.literal: Wang Wangan, prefect of Mi Province, requested more troops to attack Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wangan, prefect of Mi Province, asked for reinforcements to strike Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 詔以前沂州刺史郭瓊為東路行營都部署，帥禁軍及齊州兵赴之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed former Yizhou prefect Guo Qiong Eastern Route army deployment commander and ordered him to lead the imperial guard and Qi Province troops to the scene.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed former Yizhou prefect Guo Qiong commander of the Eastern Route army and sent him with the imperial guard and troops from Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 郭威請勒兵北臨契丹之境，詔止之。

translations.literal: Guo Wei requested to array troops and press north toward the Khitan border; an edict forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei asked to march north toward the Khitan frontier, but the court ordered him to stand down.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，遣使詣河中、鳳翔收瘞戰死及餓殍遺骸，時有僧已聚二十萬矣。

translations.literal: On bingyin, envoys were sent to Hezhong and Fengxiang to gather and bury the bones of those killed in battle and starved dead; at the time one monk had already collected two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the court sent officials to Hezhong and Fengxiang to bury the war dead and famine victims; one monk alone had already gathered two hundred thousand corpses.

sentences.zh: 唐主聞漢兵盡平三叛，始罷李金全北面行營招討使。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler, hearing that Han troops had wholly pacified the three rebellions, only then dismissed Li Jinquan as northern-route army encampment pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Later Han forces had crushed all three rebellions, the Southern Tang ruler at last removed Li Jinquan from his post as northern-route pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 唐清淮節度使劉彥貞多斂民財以賂權貴，權貴爭譽之。

translations.literal: Liu Yanzhen, Tang military governor of Qinghuai, heavily extorted the people's wealth to bribe men of power; the powerful competed to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanzhen, Southern Tang's Qinghuai military governor, squeezed the people for bribes to buy favor at court, and the powerful at court vied to praise him.

sentences.zh: 在壽州積年，恐被代，欲以警急自固，妄奏稱漢兵將大舉南伐。

translations.literal: Having accumulated years at Shouzhou, he feared replacement and wished to secure himself through alarm, falsely memorializing that Han troops would soon mount a great southern invasion.
translations.idiomatic: After years at Shouzhou he feared recall; to keep his post he invented a crisis, reporting falsely that Later Han was massing for a major southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 二月，唐主以東都留守燕王弘冀為潤、宣二州大都督，鎮潤州，寧國節度使周宗為東都留守。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Tang ruler made Eastern Capital regent Prince Yan Hongji grand commander of Run and Xuan provinces, stationed at Runzhou, and Ningguo military governor Zhou Zong Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Southern Tang ruler made Prince Yan Hongji, regent of the Eastern Capital, grand commander of Run and Xuan and posted him at Runzhou, while Ningguo military governor Zhou Zong became regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲移易籓鎮，因其請赴嘉慶節上壽，許之。

translations.literal: The court wished to transfer frontier commands and, because he requested to attend the Jiaqing Festival to offer birthday congratulations, permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court planned to shuffle the military governors and granted leave when they asked to come to court for the emperor's birthday at the Jiaqing Festival.

sentences.zh: 甲申，郭威行北邊還。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Guo Wei returned from touring the northern border.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Guo Wei came back from his inspection of the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 福州人或詣建州告唐永安留後查文徽，雲吳越兵已棄城去，請文徽為帥。

translations.literal: Some people of Fuzhou went to Jianzhou to tell Tang Yong'an acting governor Zha Wenhui that Wuyue troops had already abandoned the city and departed, and invited Wenhui to be commander.
translations.idiomatic: Men from Fuzhou came to Jianzhou and told Zha Wenhui, Southern Tang's acting governor of Yong'an, that Wuyue forces had abandoned the city and asked him to take command.

sentences.zh: 文徽信之，遣劍州刺史陳誨將水軍下閩江，文徽自以步騎繼之。

translations.literal: Wenhui believed them, dispatched Jianzhou prefect Chen Hui to lead the water force down the Min River, and Wenhui himself followed with infantry and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui believed the report. He sent Jianzhou prefect Chen Hui with the fleet down the Min River and followed with infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，水漲，誨一夕行七百里，至城下，敗福州兵，執其將馬先進等。

translations.literal: There came great rain and the waters rose; in one night Hui traveled seven hundred li, reached below the city, defeated Fuzhou troops, and captured their generals Ma Xianjin and others.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains swelled the river; Chen Hui drove his fleet seven hundred li in a single night, reached Fuzhou, routed its garrison, and captured Ma Xianjin and other commanders.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，文徽至福州，吳越知威武軍吳程詐遣數百人出迎。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Wenhui reached Fuzhou; Wu Cheng, Wuyue administrator of Weiwu Army, deceptively sent several hundred men out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Wenhui entered Fuzhou. Wu Cheng, Wuyue's administrator of Weiwu Army, sent several hundred men out in a feigned welcome.

sentences.zh: 誨曰：「閩人多詐，未可信也，宜立寨徐圖。」

translations.literal: Hui said: "The people of Min are greatly deceitful and cannot yet be trusted; we should erect a camp and plan slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui said, "The Min are treacherous—we cannot trust them yet. We should encamp and proceed with caution."

sentences.zh: 文徽曰：「疑則變生，不若乘機據其城。」

translations.literal: Wenhui said: "When doubt arises, change follows; better to seize the moment and occupy their city."
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui replied, "Hesitation breeds disaster. Better to strike now and take the city."

sentences.zh: 因引兵徑進。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led troops straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: He marched his troops straight in.

sentences.zh: 誨整眾鳴鼓，止於江湄。

translations.literal: Hui arrayed his forces, beat drums, and halted at the river's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui formed up his men, sounded the drums, and held at the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 文徽不為備，程勒兵出擊之，唐兵大敗。

translations.literal: Wenhui made no preparations; Cheng arrayed troops and struck out—Tang troops were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui took no precautions. Wu Cheng sallied and routed the Southern Tang army.

sentences.zh: 文徽墮馬，為福人所執，士卒死者萬人。

translations.literal: Wenhui fell from his horse and was seized by men of Fu; soldiers dead numbered ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhui was thrown from his horse and captured by Fuzhou men; ten thousand of his soldiers were killed.

sentences.zh: 誨全軍歸劍州。

translations.literal: Hui led the whole army back to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hui withdrew the entire fleet to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 程送文徽於錢唐，吳越王弘俶獻於五廟而釋之。

translations.literal: Cheng sent Wenhui to Qiantang; Wuyue king Hongchu presented him at the five ancestral temples and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng sent Wenhui to Qiantang, where King Hongchu of Wuyue presented him before the ancestral shrines and then released him.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，汝州奏防禦使劉審交卒。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Ruzhou reported that defense commissioner Liu Shenjiao had died.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Ruzhou reported the death of defense commissioner Liu Shenjiao.

sentences.zh: 吏民詣闕上書，以審交有仁政，乞留葬汝州，得奉事其丘壟，詔許之。

translations.literal: Officials and people went to the capital and submitted a petition, saying Shenjiao had benevolent government, begging that he be buried at Ruzhou so they could serve his mound; an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ruzhou petitioned the throne, praising Liu Shenjiao's righteous rule and asking to bury him locally so they could tend his grave; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 州人相與聚哭而葬之，以為立祠，歲時享之。

translations.literal: The people of the province together gathered in tears to bury him, made him a shrine, and offered seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the province gathered to weep at his burial, raised a shrine in his honor, and offered sacrifices each season.

sentences.zh: 太師馮道曰：「吾嘗為劉君僚佐，觀其為政，無以逾人，非能減其租賦，除其徭役也，但推公廉慈愛之心以行之耳。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Feng Dao said: "I once served as Liu Jun's subordinate official and observed his government—nothing surpassed others; he could not reduce their rent and tax or abolish their corvée labor, but only extended a heart of public integrity, compassion, and love in carrying it out.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Feng Dao said, "I once served under Liu Shenjiao and watched him govern. He did nothing extraordinary—no tax cuts, no relief from corvée—but he simply governed with public integrity and genuine compassion.

sentences.zh: 此亦眾人所能為，但他人不為而劉君獨為之，故汝人愛之如此。

translations.literal: This too is what the multitude can do, but others did not do it while Liu Jun alone did—hence the people of Ru loved him thus.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone could have done the same; others simply would not, and Liu Shenjiao alone would. That is why the people of Ruzhou loved him so.

sentences.zh: 使天下二千石皆效其所為，何患得民不如劉君哉！」

translations.literal: If throughout the realm all the two-thousand-dan officials emulated what he did, how would one worry that the people would not love them as they loved Liu Jun!"
translations.idiomatic: If every prefect in the realm followed his example, who could fail to win the people's love as Liu Shenjiao did?"

sentences.zh: 甲午，吳越丞相、昭化節度使、同平章事杜建徽卒。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Wuyue chancellor, Zhaohua military governor, and Fellow Grand Counselor Du Jianhui died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Du Jianhui, Wuyue chancellor, Zhaohua military governor, and Fellow Grand Counselor, died.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以前永興節度使越匡贊為左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: On yiwei, former Yongxing military governor Yue Kuangzan was made left Xiao Guard senior general.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, former Yongxing military governor Yue Kuangzan was appointed senior general of the Left Xiao Guard.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙午，嘉慶節，鄴都留守高行周、天平節度使慕容彥超、泰寧節度使符彥卿、昭義節度使常思、安遠節度使楊信、安國節度使薛懷讓、成德節度使武行德、彰德節度使郭瑾、保大留後王饒皆入朝。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingwu, the Jiaqing Festival—Yedu regent Gao Xingzhou, Tianping military governor Murong Yanchao, Taining military governor Fu Yanqing, Zhaoyi military governor Chang Si, Anyuan military governor Yang Xin, Anguo military governor Xue Huairang, Chengde military governor Wu Xingde, Zhangde military governor Guo Jin, and Baoda acting governor Wang Rao all entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingwu, the Jiaqing Festival, the court received Gao Xingzhou of Yedu, Murong Yanchao of Tianping, Fu Yanqing of Taining, Chang Si of Zhaoyi, Yang Xin of Anyuan, Xue Huairang of Anguo, Wu Xingde of Chengde, Guo Jin of Zhangde, and Wang Rao of Baoda.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔營寢廟於高祖長陵、世祖原陵，以時致祭。

translations.literal: On jiayin, an edict ordered construction of spirit halls at Emperor Gaozu's Changling and Emperor Shizu's Yuanling, with seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the court ordered spirit halls built at the changling of Emperor Gaozu and the yuanling of Emperor Shizu, with sacrifices at the proper seasons.

sentences.zh: 有司以費多，寢其事，以至國亡，二陵竟不沾一奠。

translations.literal: The responsible offices, citing excessive expense, shelved the matter; down to the kingdom's fall, the two tombs never received a single offering.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices balked at the cost and dropped the project; by the dynasty's fall neither tomb had ever received a single offering.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，徙高行周為天平節度使，符彥卿為平盧節度使。

translations.literal: On renxu, Gao Xingzhou was transferred to Tianping military governor; Fu Yanqing to Pinglu military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Gao Xingzhou was reassigned to Tianping and Fu Yanqing to Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 甲子，徙慕容彥超為泰寧節度使。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Murong Yanchao was transferred to Taining military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Murong Yanchao was reassigned to Taining.

sentences.zh: 永安節度使折從阮舉族入朝。

translations.literal: Yong'an military governor Zhe Congruan brought his entire clan to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yong'an military governor Zhe Congruan came to court with his whole clan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊辰朔，徙薛懷讓為匡國節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on the wuchen new moon, Xue Huairang was transferred to Kuangguo military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the wuchen new moon, Xue Huairang was reassigned to Kuangguo.

sentences.zh: 庚午，徙折從阮為武勝節度使。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Zhe Congruan was transferred to Wusheng military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Zhe Congruan was reassigned to Wusheng.

sentences.zh: 壬申，徙楊信為保大節度使，徒鎮國節度使劉詞為安國節度使，永清節度使王令溫為安遠節度使。

translations.literal: On renshen, Yang Xin was transferred to Baoda military governor; Zhenguo military governor Liu Ci to Anguo military governor; Yongqing military governor Wang Lingwen to Anyuan military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Yang Xin went to Baoda, Liu Ci from Zhenguo to Anguo, and Wang Lingwen from Yongqing to Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 李守貞之亂，王饒潛與之通。

translations.literal: During Li Shouzhen's rebellion, Wang Rao secretly communicated with him.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Shouzhen's rebellion, Wang Rao had secretly colluded with him.

sentences.zh: 守貞平，眾謂饒必居散地。

translations.literal: When Shouzhen was pacified, the multitude said Rao would surely be placed in an inactive post.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shouzhen fell, everyone expected Wang Rao to be stripped of real command.

sentences.zh: 及入朝，厚結史弘肇，遷護國節度使，聞者駭之。

translations.literal: When he entered court, he lavishly cultivated Shi Hongzhao and was transferred to Huguo military governor; hearers were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he came to court he lavishly cultivated Shi Hongzhao and was made Huguo military governor—a move that shocked all who heard it.

sentences.zh: 楊邠求解樞密使，帝遣中使諭止之。

translations.literal: Yang Bin requested release from the post of Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner; the emperor sent a palace envoy to instruct and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin asked to resign as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; the emperor sent a palace envoy to refuse the request.

sentences.zh: 宣徽北院使吳虔裕在旁曰：「樞密重地，難以久居，當使後來者迭為之，相公辭之是也。」

translations.literal: Xuannorth court commissioner Wu Qianyu, standing beside, said: "The Bureau of Military Affairs is a weighty post, hard to hold long; later men should rotate in it—the grand counselor's resignation is right."
translations.idiomatic: Xuannorth court commissioner Wu Qianyu, standing nearby, said, "The Bureau of Military Affairs is too weighty a post to hold indefinitely; successors should rotate through it. The Grand Counselor is right to resign."

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，不悅，辛巳，以虔裕為鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing this, was displeased; on xinsi, Qianyu was made Zhengzhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense. On xinsi he demoted Wu Qianyu to defense commissioner of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以契丹近入寇，橫行河北，諸籓鎮各自守，無扞御之者，議以郭威鎮鄴都，使督諸將以備契丹。

translations.literal: The court, because the Khitan had recently invaded and ranged freely through Hebei while the frontier commands each held to themselves with none to repel them, deliberated placing Guo Wei at Yedu to supervise the generals against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: With Khitan raiders ranging freely through Hebei while the military governors each looked only to their own defense, the court decided to post Guo Wei at Yedu to command the northern frontier against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 史弘肇欲威仍領樞密使，蘇逢吉以為故事無之，弘肇曰：「領樞密使則可以便宜從事，諸軍畏服，號令行矣。」

translations.literal: Shi Hongzhao wished Guo Wei still to hold the Bureau of Military Affairs commission; Su Fengji held that precedent had none of this. Hongzhao said: "Holding the Bureau of Military Affairs commission, one can act expediently at discretion; the armies fear and submit, and orders go forth."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao wanted Guo Wei to keep the Bureau of Military Affairs commission. Su Fengji objected that precedent knew no such arrangement. Hongzhao replied, "With that commission he can act on his own authority—the armies will obey, and orders will be carried out."

sentences.zh: 帝卒從弘肇議。

translations.literal: The emperor finally followed Hongzhao's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Shi Hongzhao in the end.

sentences.zh: 弘肇怨逢吉異議，逢吉曰：「以內制外，順也；

translations.literal: Hongzhao resented Fengji's differing opinion. Fengji said: "Using the inner to control the outer—this accords with reason;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao resented Su Fengji's dissent. Su Fengji said, "It is natural for the inner court to control the outer frontier—

sentences.zh: 今反以外制內，其可乎！」

translations.literal: now to reverse and use the outer to control the inner—can this be permitted!"
translations.idiomatic: but to let the frontier commander control the inner court—how can that be right?"

sentences.zh: 壬午，制以威為鄴都留守、天雄節度使，樞密使如故。

translations.literal: On renwu, by decree Guo Wei was made Yedu regent and Tianxiong military governor, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner as before.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the court appointed Guo Wei regent of Yedu and Tianxiong military governor while retaining his Bureau of Military Affairs commission.

sentences.zh: 仍詔河北，兵甲錢穀，但見郭威文書立皆稟應。

translations.literal: Further an edict to Hebei: arms, armor, funds, and grain—whatever document appeared from Guo Wei, all were to be supplied at once.
translations.idiomatic: An edict further ordered that throughout Hebei arms, funds, and grain were to be supplied immediately upon any document from Guo Wei.

sentences.zh: 明日，朝貴會飲於竇貞固之第，弘肇舉大觴屬威，厲聲曰：「昨日廷議，一何同異！

translations.literal: The next day, court nobles met to drink at Dou Zhengzhai's residence; Hongzhao raised a great goblet and addressed Wei, voice harsh: "Yesterday's court deliberation—how greatly at odds!
translations.idiomatic: The next day the high officials met for wine at Dou Zhengzhai's house. Shi Hongzhao raised a great cup to Guo Wei and said sharply, "Yesterday's deliberation—what sharp differences!

sentences.zh: 今日為弟飲之。」

translations.literal: Today I drink for my younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: Today I drink to you, my brother."

sentences.zh: 逢吉與楊邠亦舉觴曰：「是國家之事，何足介意！」

translations.literal: Fengji and Yang Bin also raised goblets and said: "This is the state's affair—what need to take it to heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji and Yang Bin raised their cups as well and said, "This concerns the state—why take it so personally?"

sentences.zh: 弘肇又厲聲曰：「安定國家，在長槍大劍，安用毛錐！」

translations.literal: Hongzhao again in harsh voice said: "Stabilizing the state lies in long spears and great swords—what use for hair awls!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao thundered again, "The state is secured by long spears and great swords—not by brush pens!"

sentences.zh: 王章曰：「無毛錐，則財賦何從可出？」

translations.literal: Wang Zhang said: "Without hair awls, whence can revenue and levies come forth?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang retorted, "Without brush pens, whence would revenue come?"

sentences.zh: 自是，將相始有隙。

translations.literal: From this, generals and chancellors first had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the generals and the chancellors were divided.

sentences.zh: 癸未，罷永安軍。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Yong'an Army was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the court abolished Yong'an Army.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以左監門衛將軍郭榮為貴州刺史、天雄牙內都指揮使。

translations.literal: On renchen, left Jianmen Guard general Guo Rong was made Guizhou prefect and Tianxiong inner garrison commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Guo Rong, general of the Left Jianmen Guard, was made prefect of Guizhou and inner commander of the Tianxiong garrison.

sentences.zh: 榮本姓柴，父守禮，郭威之妻兄也，威未有子時養以為子。

translations.literal: Rong's original surname was Chai; his father Shouli was Guo Wei's wife's elder brother; when Wei had no son he adopted Rong as his son.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Rong was born a Chai; his father Shouli was Guo Wei's brother-in-law. Guo Wei adopted him when he had no heir of his own.

sentences.zh: 五月，己亥，以府州蕃漢馬步都指揮使折德扆為本州團練使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jihai, Fuzhou Tang and Han horse and foot commander-in-chief Zhe Deyi was made regimental trainer of that province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jihai, Zhe Deyi, combined Tang and Han cavalry and infantry commander of Fuzhou, was made regimental trainer of that province.

sentences.zh: 德扆，從阮之子也。

translations.literal: Deyi was Congruan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Deyi was the son of Zhe Congruan.

sentences.zh: 庚子，郭威辭行，言於帝曰：「太后從先帝久，多歷天下事，陛下富於春秋，有事宜稟其教而行之。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Guo Wei took leave to depart and said to the emperor: "The Empress Dowager followed the late emperor long and has passed through many affairs of the realm; Your Majesty is rich in youth—in affairs one should receive her instruction and act accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, as Guo Wei prepared to depart, he told the emperor, "The Empress Dowager served the late emperor for many years and knows the realm's affairs. Your Majesty is still young; in weighty matters defer to her counsel.

sentences.zh: 親近忠直，放遠讒邪，善惡之間，所宜明審。

translations.literal: Draw near the loyal and straight, send far the slanderous and corrupt; between good and evil, one should discern clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Keep loyal men close, keep slanderers at a distance, and judge good and evil with clear eyes.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉、楊邠、史弘肇皆先帝舊臣，盡忠徇國，願陛下推心任之，必無敗失。

translations.literal: Su Fengji, Yang Bin, and Shi Hongzhao are all the late emperor's old ministers, exhaustingly loyal and sacrificing for the state; I wish Your Majesty to open your heart and employ them—surely without defeat or loss.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji, Yang Bin, and Shi Hongzhao are the late emperor's loyal ministers. Trust them fully and you will not go wrong.

sentences.zh: 至於疆場之事，臣願竭其愚駑，庶不負驅策。」

translations.literal: As for frontier affairs, your servant wishes to exhaust his dull competence, that he may not fail the whip and spur."
translations.idiomatic: As for the frontier, I will do all that my poor talents allow, and not fail the task you set me."

sentences.zh: 帝斂容謝之。

translations.literal: The emperor composed his expression and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed himself and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 威至鄴都，以河北困弊，戒邊將謹守疆場，嚴守備，無得出侵掠，契丹入寇，則堅壁清野以待之。

translations.literal: When Wei reached Yedu, because Hebei was exhausted and impoverished, he admonished the frontier generals to carefully guard the borders, strictly maintain defenses, and not go out to raid; when the Khitan invaded, then hold fast within walls and clear the countryside to await them.
translations.idiomatic: At Yedu, seeing Hebei's exhaustion, Guo Wei ordered his frontier commanders to hold their lines, strengthen defenses, and refrain from raiding; if the Khitan invaded, they were to fortify the walls and strip the countryside bare and wait.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，敕：「防禦、團練使，自非軍期，無得專奏事，皆先申觀察使斟酌以聞。」

translations.literal: On xinchou, an edict: "Defense and regimental training commissioners, except in military emergencies, may not solely memorialize affairs—all must first report to the surveillance commissioner for deliberation before it reaches the throne."
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou an edict ruled that defense and regimental training commissioners, except in wartime, could not memorialize the throne directly but must first submit reports through their surveillance commissioners."

sentences.zh: 丙午，以皇弟山南西道節度使承勳為開封尹，加兼中書令，實未出閣。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the emperor's younger brother, Shannan West Circuit military governor Chengxun, was made Kaifeng Intendant, additionally Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs—in fact he had not yet left the palace apartments.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor's younger brother Chengxun, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, was named Kaifeng Intendant and given the additional title of Director of the Department of State Affairs, though he had not yet formally left the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使劉銖，貪虐恣橫，朝廷欲征之，恐其拒命，因沂、密用兵於唐，遣前沂州刺史郭瓊將兵屯青州。

translations.literal: Pinglu military governor Liu Zhu, greedy, cruel, and willfully overbearing—the court wished to summon him but feared he would refuse the command; because troops were being used against Tang at Yi and Mi, former Yizhou prefect Guo Qiong was sent to encamp troops at Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhu, military governor of Pinglu, was greedy and brutal. The court wished to recall him but feared defiance; using the campaign against Southern Tang in Yi and Mi as cover, it sent former Yizhou prefect Guo Qiong to encamp at Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 銖不自安，置酒召瓊，伏兵幕下，欲害之。

translations.literal: Zhu was ill at ease, set out wine and summoned Qiong, with ambush troops beneath the tent curtain, intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhu, uneasy, invited Guo Qiong to a banquet and hid assassins in the tent.

sentences.zh: 瓊知其謀，悉屏左右，從容如會，了無懼色，銖不敢發。

translations.literal: Qiong knew his plot, dismissed all attendants, attended at ease as at a meeting, entirely without fear—Zhu dared not spring it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qiong saw through the plot, dismissed his escort, and entered alone without the least sign of fear; Liu Zhu dared not strike.

sentences.zh: 瓊因諭以禍福，銖感服，詔至即行。

translations.literal: Qiong then instructed him on fortune and disaster; Zhu was moved and submitted; when the edict arrived he departed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qiong reasoned with him on the consequences; Liu Zhu was persuaded and obeyed the summons at once when it came.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，銖入朝。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Zhu entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Liu Zhu arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以瓊為穎州團練使。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Qiong was made Yingzhou regimental trainer.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Guo Qiong was made regimental trainer of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，王章置酒會諸朝貴，酒酣，為手勢令，史弘肇不閒其事，客省使閻晉卿坐次弘肇，屢教之。

translations.literal: On guichou, Wang Zhang set out wine and gathered the court nobles; when wine was deep they played hand-gesture commands; Shi Hongzhao was unversed in the matter; guest-reception commissioner Yan Jinqing sat next to Hongzhao and repeatedly instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Wang Zhang hosted the high officials. Deep in wine they played hand-signal drinking games; Shi Hongzhao did not know the rules, and guest-reception commissioner Yan Jinqing, seated beside him, kept explaining them.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉戲之曰：「旁有姓閻人，何憂罰爵！」

translations.literal: Su Fengji jested to him: "Beside you is a man surnamed Yan—what worry of penalty cups!"
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji teased, "With a Yan beside you, why fear drinking penalties!"

sentences.zh: 弘肇妻閻氏，本酒家倡也，意逢吉譏之，大怒，以丑語詬逢吉，逢吉不應。

translations.literal: Hongzhao's wife was surnamed Yan, originally a tavern songstress; he took it that Fengji was mocking him, was greatly angered, and reviled Fengji with foul words; Fengji did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao's wife, née Yan, had been a tavern singer; he took Su Fengji's remark as a slight, flew into a rage, and showered him with abuse. Su Fengji did not reply.

sentences.zh: 弘肇欲毆之，逢吉起去。

translations.literal: Hongzhao wished to beat him; Fengji rose and left.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao moved to strike him; Su Fengji rose and walked away.

sentences.zh: 弘肇索劍欲追之，楊邠泣止之曰：「蘇公宰相，公若殺之，置天子何地，願孰思之！」

translations.literal: Hongzhao sought a sword to pursue him; Yang Bin wept and stopped him, saying: "Grand Counselor Su—if you kill him, where does that leave the Son of Heaven? I beg you weigh this carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao grabbed for a sword to chase him down. Yang Bin wept and held him back: "Su Fengji is a chancellor. If you kill him, what becomes of the throne? Think carefully!"

sentences.zh: 弘肇即上馬去，邠與之聯鑣，送至其第而還。

translations.literal: Hongzhao immediately mounted and departed; Bin rode alongside him, escorted him to his residence, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao mounted and rode off; Yang Bin rode beside him to his gate and then returned.

sentences.zh: 於是將相如水火矣。

translations.literal: At this the generals and chancellors were like water and fire.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the generals and chancellors were at open enmity.

sentences.zh: 帝使宣徽使王峻置酒和解之，不能得。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Xuann commissioner Wang Jun to set out wine and reconcile them; he could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xuann commissioner Wang Jun to host a reconciliation banquet, but failed.

sentences.zh: 逢吉欲求出鎮以避之，既而中止，曰：「吾去朝廷，止煩史公一處分，吾齏粉矣！」

translations.literal: Fengji wished to seek a provincial post to avoid this; then he stopped, saying: "If I leave the court, one word from Lord Shi would suffice—I would be ground to powder!"
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji considered asking for a provincial post to escape Shi Hongzhao, then changed his mind: "If I leave court, one word from Shi Hongzhao would be enough to have me ground to dust."

sentences.zh: 王章亦忽忽不樂，欲求外官，楊、史固止之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang was also gloomy and unhappy, wished to seek an outer office; Yang and Shi firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang too grew despondent and wanted a post outside the capital; Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao firmly dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 閏月，宮中數有怪。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, within the palace there were repeated strangenesses.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month the palace was troubled by repeated omens.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，大風雨，發屋拔木，吹鄭門扉起，十餘步而落。

translations.literal: On guisi, great wind and rain blew off roofs and uprooted trees, blew the Zheng Gate leaves upward, and they fell after more than ten paces.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi a violent storm tore off roofs and uprooted trees and lifted the leaves of the Zheng Gate a dozen paces before they fell.

sentences.zh: 震死者六七人，水深平地尺餘。

translations.literal: Those struck dead by lightning numbered six or seven; water depth on level ground was more than a foot.
translations.idiomatic: Lightning killed six or seven people; a foot of water stood on level ground.

sentences.zh: 帝召司天監趙延乂，問以禳祈之術，對曰：「臣之業在天文時日，禳祈非所習也。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Directorate of Astronomy Zhao Yanyi and asked about techniques of exorcism and prayer; he replied: "Your servant's craft lies in astronomy and calendar dates; exorcism and prayer are not what I have studied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhao Yanyi of the Directorate of Astronomy and asked how to avert the disasters. Yanyi replied, "My craft is astronomy and calendrics; ritual exorcism is not my field.

sentences.zh: 然王者欲弭災異，莫如修德。」

translations.literal: Yet if a king wishes to quell disasters and anomalies, nothing surpasses cultivating virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Yet if a ruler wishes to still heaven's warnings, nothing avails like cultivating virtue."

sentences.zh: 延乂歸，帝遣中使問：「如何為修德？」

translations.literal: Yanyi returned; the emperor sent a palace envoy to ask: "How does one cultivate virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: After Yanyi withdrew, the emperor sent a palace envoy to ask, "What does cultivating virtue mean?"

sentences.zh: 延乂對：「請讀《貞觀政要》而法之。」

translations.literal: Yanyi replied: "I beg that you read the Essentials of Governance of the Zhenguan Era and take it as model."
translations.idiomatic: Yanyi answered, "Read the Essentials of Governance of the Zhenguan Era and govern accordingly."

sentences.zh: 六月，河決鄭州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Yellow River burst its banks at Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Yellow River broke through its banks at Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 馬希萼既敗歸，乃以書誘辰、漵州及梅山蠻，欲與共擊湖南。

translations.literal: Ma Xie, having been defeated and returned, then by letter enticed Chen and Xu provinces and the Meishan barbarians, wishing to join in striking Hunan together.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie, defeated and driven home, wrote to the prefectures of Chen and Xu and the Meishan tribes, urging them to join him in striking Hunan.

sentences.zh: 蠻素聞長沙帑藏之富，大喜，爭出兵赴之，遂攻益陽。

translations.literal: The barbarians had long heard of Changsha treasury's wealth, were greatly pleased, vied to send troops to join, and then attacked Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes, hearing of Changsha's rich treasury, were delighted and rushed to join; together they attacked Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 楚王希廣遣指揮使陳璠拒之，戰於淹溪，璠敗死。

translations.literal: Chu king Xiguang dispatched commander Chen Fan to resist; they fought at Yanxi; Fan was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiguang of Chu sent commander Chen Fan to resist them; at Yanxi Chen Fan was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，唐歸馬先進等於吳越以易查文徽。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, Tang returned Ma Xianjin and others to Wuyue in exchange for Zha Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Southern Tang returned Ma Xianjin and the other captives to Wuyue in exchange for Zha Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 馬希萼又遣群蠻攻迪田，八月，戊戌，破之，殺其鎮將張延嗣。

translations.literal: Ma Xie again sent the mass of barbarians to attack Ditan; in the eighth month, on wuxu, they broke it and killed its garrison commander Zhang Yansi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie sent the tribal forces against Ditan again; on wuxu in the eighth month they took the town and killed garrison commander Zhang Yansi.

sentences.zh: 楚王希廣遣指揮使黃處超救之，處超敗死。

translations.literal: Chu king Xiguang dispatched commander Huang Chuchao to rescue; Chuchao was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiguang of Chu sent Huang Chuchao to the rescue; Huang Chuchao was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 潭人震恐，復遣牙內指揮使崔洪璉將兵七千屯玉潭。

translations.literal: The people of Tan were shaken in fear; he again dispatched inner-garrison commander Cui Honglian to lead seven thousand troops to encamp at Yutan.
translations.idiomatic: Changsha trembled; Xiguang sent inner-garrison commander Cui Honglian with seven thousand men to encamp at Yutan.

sentences.zh: 庚子，蜀主立其弟仕毅為夔王，仁贄為雅王，仁裕為彭王，仁操為嘉王。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Shu ruler enfeoffed his younger brother Shirong as Prince of Kui, Renzan as Prince of Ya, Renyu as Prince of Peng, and Rencao as Prince of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Shu ruler enfeoffed his brothers Shirong as Prince of Kui, Renzan as Prince of Ya, Renyu as Prince of Peng, and Rencao as Prince of Jia.

sentences.zh: 己酉，立子玄喆為秦王，玄玨為褒王。

translations.literal: On jiyou, he enfeoffed his sons Xuanzhe as Prince of Qin and Xuanjue as Prince of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou he enfeoffed his sons Xuanzhe as Prince of Qin and Xuanjue as Prince of Bao.

sentences.zh: 晉李太后在建州，臥病，無醫藥，惟與晉主仰天號泣，戟手罵杜重威、李守貞曰：「吾死不置汝！」

translations.literal: Jin Empress Dowager Li at Jianzhou, bedridden, without medicine or physicians, only with the Jin ruler looked up to heaven and wailed, fingers crossed in curse reviling Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen: "I will not leave you even in death!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Li of Jin lay ill at Jianzhou without medicine or doctors; she and the Jin ruler could only weep heavenward and curse Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen: "I will haunt you beyond the grave!"

sentences.zh: 戊午，卒。

translations.literal: On wuwu, she died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu she died.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，有自契丹來者云：「晉主及馮後尚無恙，其從者亡歸及物故則過半矣。」

translations.literal: In Zhou's Xiande era, one who came from the Khitan said: "The Jin ruler and Empress Feng are still without harm; of his followers those who fled back and those who died exceed half."
translations.idiomatic: During Later Zhou's Xiande era a traveler from the Khitan reported, "The Jin ruler and Empress Feng were still alive, but more than half their followers had fled or perished."

sentences.zh: 馬希萼表請別置進奏務於京師。

translations.literal: Ma Xie memorialized requesting a separate memorial office be established at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie petitioned to establish a separate memorial office at the Later Han capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛巳，詔以湖南已有進奏務，不許。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinsi, an edict held that Hunan already had a memorial office and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinsi, the court refused, noting that Hunan already had a memorial office at court.

sentences.zh: 亦賜楚王希廣詔，勸以敦睦。

translations.literal: Also an edict was bestowed on Chu king Xiguang, urging cordial harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The court also sent King Xiguang of Chu an edict urging brotherly concord.

sentences.zh: 馬希萼以朝廷意佑楚王希廣，怒，遣使稱籓於唐，乞師攻楚。

translations.literal: Ma Xie, taking that the court favored Chu king Xiguang, was angered, sent envoys to declare vassalage to Tang, and begged troops to attack Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie, believing the court favored his brother, sent envoys to declare vassalage to Southern Tang and begged for troops to strike Chu.

sentences.zh: 唐加希萼同平章事，以鄂州今年租稅賜之，命楚州刺史何敬洙將兵助希萼。

translations.literal: Tang added Xie as Fellow Grand Counselor, granted him Ezhou's rent and tax for the year, and ordered Chuzhou prefect He Jingzhu to lead troops to aid Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang made Ma Xie Fellow Grand Counselor, granted him Ezhou's annual revenue, and ordered Chuzhou prefect He Jingzhu to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙午，希廣遣使上表告急，言：「荊南、嶺南、江南連謀，欲分湖南之地，乞發兵屯澧州，以扼江南、荊南援朗州之路。」

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, on bingwu, Xiguang sent envoys with a memorial reporting emergency, saying: "Jingnan, Lingnan, and Jiangnan are allied in plot, wishing to divide Hunan's territory; I beg troops be sent to encamp at Lizhou to choke the routes by which Jiangnan and Jingnan would aid Langzhou."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingwu, Xiguang sent an urgent memorial: "Jingnan, Lingnan, and Jiangnan conspire to carve up Hunan. Send troops to Lizhou to block their lines of relief to Langzhou."

sentences.zh: 丁未，以吳越王弘俶為諸道兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Wuyue king Hongchu was made commander-in-chief of all circuits' armies and horses.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei King Hongchu of Wuyue was named supreme commander of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 楚王希廣以朗州與山蠻入寇，諸將屢敗，憂形於色。

translations.literal: Chu king Xiguang, because Langzhou and the mountain barbarians invaded, his generals repeatedly defeated, had worry show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: With Langzhou and the mountain tribes raiding and his generals repeatedly defeated, King Xiguang's face showed his dread.

sentences.zh: 劉彥瑫言於希廣曰：「朗州兵不滿萬，馬不滿千，都府精兵十萬，何憂不勝！

translations.literal: Liu Yanchuang spoke to Xiguang: "Langzhou's troops do not reach ten thousand, horses not reach a thousand; the capital's elite troops are one hundred thousand—what worry of not prevailing!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanchuang told Xiguang, "Langzhou has fewer than ten thousand men and a thousand horses. The capital commands a hundred thousand elites—how can we fail?

sentences.zh: 願假臣兵萬餘人，戰艦百五十艘，逕入朗州縛取希萼，以解大王之憂。」

translations.literal: I wish to borrow more than ten thousand troops under your servant and one hundred fifty warships, enter Langzhou directly and bind Xie, to resolve the great king's worry."
translations.idiomatic: Grant me ten thousand men and a hundred fifty warships, and I will march straight into Langzhou, seize Ma Xie, and lift this burden from Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 王悅，以彥瑫為戰棹都指揮使、朗州行營都統。

translations.literal: The king was pleased and made Yanchuang war-fleet commander-in-chief and Langzhou campaign army commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang was pleased and made Liu Yanchuang commander of the war fleet and overall commander of the Langzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 彥瑫入朗州境，父老爭以牛酒犒軍，曰：「百姓不願從亂，望都府之兵久矣！」

translations.literal: Yanchuang entered Langzhou territory; elders vied to offer oxen and wine to reward the army, saying: "The common people do not wish to follow rebellion; they have long awaited the capital's troops!"
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Yanchuang entered Langzhou territory, elders vied to bring cattle and wine, saying, "We have waited long for the capital's army—we want no part of rebellion."

sentences.zh: 彥瑫厚賞之。

translations.literal: Yanchuang richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanchuang rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 戰艦過，則運竹木以斷其後。

translations.literal: When the warships passed, they hauled bamboo and timber to sever the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Once the fleet had passed, they felled bamboo and timber to block the river behind it.

sentences.zh: 是日，馬希萼遣朗兵及蠻兵六千、戰艦百艘逆戰於湄州。

translations.literal: That day, Ma Xie dispatched Langzhou troops and six thousand barbarian troops and one hundred warships to meet in battle at Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Ma Xie sent six thousand Langzhou and tribal troops with a hundred warships to meet Liu Yanchuang at Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 彥瑫乘風縱火以焚其艦，頃之，風回，反自焚。

translations.literal: Yanchuang rode the wind to set fire and burn their ships; shortly the wind turned and burned himself instead.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanchuang tried to burn the enemy fleet with the wind at his back; moments later the wind shifted and his own ships caught fire.

sentences.zh: 彥瑫還走，江路已斷，士卒戰及溺死者數千人。

translations.literal: Yanchuang turned and fled; the river route was already cut; soldiers killed in battle and drowned numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanchuang fled; the river behind him was blocked; thousands of his men were killed or drowned.

sentences.zh: 希廣聞之，涕泣不知所為。

translations.literal: Xiguang, hearing this, wept tears and knew not what to do.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiguang heard the news he wept, helpless.

sentences.zh: 希廣平日罕頒賜，至是，大出金帛以取悅於士卒。

translations.literal: Xiguang on ordinary days rarely distributed rewards; at this point he greatly disbursed gold and silk to win the soldiers' pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang, who seldom rewarded his men, now lavished gold and silk to regain their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 或告天策左司馬希崇流言惑眾，反狀已明，請殺之。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Left Tiance marshal Xichong spread rumors to confuse the masses, evidence of rebellion already clear, and requested he be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Left Tiance marshal Ma Xichong was stirring sedition and clearly plotting rebellion, and urged his execution.

sentences.zh: 希廣曰：「吾自害其弟，何以見先王於地下！」

translations.literal: Xiguang said: "If I myself harm my younger brother, how can I face the former king beneath the earth!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang said, "If I kill my own brother, how shall I face our father in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 馬軍指揮使張暉將兵自他道擊朗州，至龍陽，聞彥瑫敗，退屯益陽。

translations.literal: Horse-army commander Zhang Hui led troops by another route to strike Langzhou; reaching Longyang, hearing Yanchuang defeated, withdrew to encamp at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry commander Zhang Hui marched on Langzhou by another route; at Longyang he heard of Liu Yanchuang's defeat and fell back to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 希萼又遣指揮使朱進忠等將兵三千急攻益陽，張暉紿其眾曰：「我以麾下出賊後，汝輩留城中待我，相與合勢擊之。」

translations.literal: Xie again dispatched commander Zhu Jinzhong and others to lead three thousand troops in urgent attack on Yiyang; Zhang Hui deceived his troops saying: "I will take my personal followers out behind the bandits; you remain in the city awaiting me—we together will combine force and strike them."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie sent Zhu Jinzhong with three thousand men to storm Yiyang. Zhang Hui told his troops, "I will circle behind the enemy; hold the city and wait—we will crush them together."

sentences.zh: 既出，遂自竹頭市遁歸長沙。

translations.literal: Once out, he then from Zhutou market escaped and returned to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Once outside the walls he fled through Zhutou market back to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 朗兵知城中無主，急擊之，士卒九千餘人皆死。

translations.literal: Langzhou troops, knowing the city had no master, pressed the attack; soldiers numbering more than nine thousand all died.
translations.idiomatic: The Langzhou troops, finding the city leaderless, pressed the attack; more than nine thousand defenders were killed.

sentences.zh: 吳越王弘俶歸查文徽於唐，文徽得喑疾，以工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Wuyue king Hongchu returned Zha Wenhui to Tang; Wenhui contracted mute illness and retired as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: King Hongchu of Wuyue returned Zha Wenhui to Southern Tang; Wenhui had been struck mute and retired as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the jiazi new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the jiazi new moon, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 蜀太師、中書令宋忠武王趙廷隱卒。

translations.literal: Shu Grand Preceptor and Director of the Department of State Affairs Song Loyal and Martial King Zhao Tingyin died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin, Shu Grand Preceptor, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Prince Song the Loyal and Martial, died.

sentences.zh: 楚王希廣遣其僚屬孟駢說馬希萼曰：「公忘父兄之仇，北面事唐，何異袁譚求救於曹公邪！」

translations.literal: Chu king Xiguang sent his staff member Meng Pian to persuade Ma Xie: "You forget father and elder brother's enmity and face north to serve Tang—how does this differ from Yuan Tan begging rescue from Lord Cao!"
translations.idiomatic: King Xiguang of Chu sent his officer Meng Pian to reason with Ma Xie: "You forget your father's blood feud and bow north to Southern Tang—are you not Yuan Tan begging Cao Cao for aid?"

sentences.zh: 希萼將斬之，駢曰：「古者兵交，使在其間，駢若愛死，安肯此來！

translations.literal: Xie was about to behead him; Pian said: "In antiquity when armies crossed, envoys moved among them—if Pian cherished death, how would he willingly come here!
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie moved to execute him. Meng Pian said, "When armies clash, envoys pass between them. If I feared death, I would never have come.

sentences.zh: 駢之言非私於潭人，實為公謀也。」

translations.literal: Pian's words are not private to the people of Tan; they are truly for your lordship's planning."
translations.idiomatic: I speak not for Changsha alone but in your own interest."

sentences.zh: 乃釋之，使還報曰：「大義絕矣，非地下不相見也！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he released him and had him return with the report: "Great righteousness is severed—it is not that we shall not meet beneath the earth!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie spared him and sent him back with the reply: "All bonds of duty are broken—but we shall meet again in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 朱進忠請希萼自將兵取潭州，辛未，希萼留其子光贊守朗州，悉發境內之兵趣長沙，自稱順天王。

translations.literal: Zhu Jinchong asked Xi'e to personally lead troops to take Tanzhou. On xinsi, Xi'e left his son Guangzan to guard Langzhou, mobilized all troops within his territory toward Changsha, and styled himself King Who Obeys Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jinchong urged Xi'e to lead the army himself against Tanzhou. On the xinsi day, Xi'e left his son Guangzan at Langzhou, called up every soldier in his domain, marched on Changsha, and proclaimed himself the King Who Obeys Heaven.

sentences.zh: 詔侍衛步軍都指揮使、寧江節度使王殷將兵屯澶州以備契丹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Palace Attendant Infantry Commander and Ningjiang Military Governor Wang Yin to lead troops and encamp at Danzhou to guard against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Wang Yin, Palace Attendant Infantry Commander and military governor of Ningjiang, to camp at Danzhou with his troops against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 殷，瀛州人也。

translations.literal: Yin was a man of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin was from Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議發兵，以安遠節度使王令溫為都部署，以救潭州，會內難作，不果。

translations.literal: The court deliberated dispatching troops, appointing Anyuan Military Governor Wang Lingwen as overall commander to rescue Tanzhou, but when internal turmoil arose, it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: The court planned to send an army under Wang Lingwen of Anyuan to relieve Tanzhou, but domestic crisis intervened and the expedition never happened.

sentences.zh: 帝自即位以來，樞密使、右僕射、同平章事楊邠總機政，樞密使兼侍中郭威主征伐，歸德節度使、侍衛親軍都指揮使兼中書令史弘肇典宿衛，三司使、同平章事王章掌財賦。

translations.literal: Since the Emperor's accession, Privy Council Director, Right Vice Director, and Chief Councilor Yang Bin had overseen state affairs; Privy Council Director and Palace Attendant Guo Wei directed campaigns; Guide Military Governor, Palace Attendant Personal Guard Commander, and Chief Councilor Shi Hongzhao commanded the palace guard; Three Departments Commissioner and Chief Councilor Wang Zhang managed finances.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he took the throne, four men ran the Later Han: Yang Bin held the privy council and chief ministry; Guo Wei commanded the armies; Shi Hongzhao, also chief councilor, held the palace guard; Wang Zhang, likewise chief councilor, held the purse.

sentences.zh: 邠頗公忠，退朝，門無私謁，雖不卻四方饋遺，有餘輒獻之。

translations.literal: Bin was notably fair and loyal. After court, his gate knew no private callers. Though he did not refuse gifts from all quarters, any surplus he turned over.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin was conscientious and upright. After audience he admitted no private petitioners. He accepted gifts from the provinces but sent whatever remained to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 弘肇督察京城，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: Hongzhao inspected the capital; no one picked up lost things on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shi Hongzhao's policing, lost property lay untouched in the streets of the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時承契丹蕩覆之餘，公私困竭，章捃摭遺利，吝於出納，以實府庫。

translations.literal: At that time, coming after Khitan devastation, public and private resources were exhausted. Zhang scraped up hidden profits, stingy in disbursement, to fill the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: The realm still reeled from Khitan destruction, public coffers and private stores alike drained dry. Wang Zhang squeezed every hidden profit from the economy, tight-fisted in spending, until the vaults swelled.

sentences.zh: 屬三叛連衡，宿兵累年而供饋不乏。

translations.literal: When the three rebellions allied, troops were stationed for years yet supplies did not fail.
translations.idiomatic: Through three linked rebellions and years of encamped armies, provisions never ran out.

sentences.zh: 及事平，賜予之外，尚有餘積，以是國家粗安。

translations.literal: When matters were settled, beyond rewards there remained surplus; thus the state achieved rough stability.
translations.idiomatic: When peace returned, rewards were paid and money still remained. The dynasty had a measure of stability.

sentences.zh: 章聚斂刻急。

translations.literal: Zhang's exactions were harsh and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang's levies were relentless.

sentences.zh: 舊制，田稅每斛更輸二升，謂之「雀鼠耗」，章始令更輸二斗，謂之「省耗」；

translations.literal: Under the old system, each bushel of field tax required an additional two sheng, called "sparrow-and-rat loss." Zhang first ordered an additional two dou, calling it "saving loss."
translations.idiomatic: By custom each bushel of grain tax carried two extra sheng—the "sparrow-and-rat allowance." Zhang raised it to two dou and called the levy "saving loss."

sentences.zh: 舊錢出入皆以八十為陌，章台令入者八十，出者七十七，謂之「省陌」；

translations.literal: Old coinage counted eighty per string both in and out. Zhang's office ordered eighty on intake and seventy-seven on payout, calling it "saving strings."
translations.idiomatic: Coins had always traded at eighty cash to the string, whether paid in or paid out. Zhang's office kept eighty on receipts and paid seventy-seven on disbursements, calling the difference "saving strings."

sentences.zh: 有犯鹽、麴、酒麴之禁，錙銖涓滴，罪皆死；

translations.literal: Violations of the salt, yeast, and liquor monopolies—even a speck or drop—were punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: Breaches of the salt, yeast, or liquor monopolies—down to the last grain or drop—were capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 由是百姓愁怨。

translations.literal: Because of this the common people groaned with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 章尤不喜文臣，嘗曰：「此輩授之握算，不知縱橫，何益於用！」

translations.literal: Zhang especially disliked civil officials. He once said: "Give these fellows an abacus and they cannot tell east from west—what good are they!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang despised the literati. "Hand these men an abacus," he said once, "and they cannot tell east from west. Of what use are they?"

sentences.zh: 俸祿皆以不堪資軍者給之，吏已高其估，章更增之。

translations.literal: Salaries were paid in goods unfit for army use. Officials had already inflated their valuations, and Zhang raised them further.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries came in goods unfit for the army. Officials had already marked up their value; Zhang marked them up again.

sentences.zh: 帝左右嬖倖浸用事，太后親戚亦干預朝政，邠等屢裁抑之。

translations.literal: The Emperor's favored attendants gradually gained influence, and the Empress Dowager's kin also meddled in court affairs. Bin and the others repeatedly checked them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favorites grew bolder, and the empress dowager's relatives meddled in policy. Yang Bin and his colleagues checked them again and again.

sentences.zh: 太后有故人子求補軍職，弘肇怒而斬之。

translations.literal: An old acquaintance of the Empress Dowager asked her son for a military appointment. Hongzhao flew into a rage and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: An old friend of the empress dowager secured a military post for her son. Shi Hongzhao cut off his head in fury.

sentences.zh: 武德使李業，太后之弟也，高祖使掌內帑，帝即位，尤蒙寵任。

translations.literal: Military Virtue Commissioner Li Ye, the Empress Dowager's younger brother, had been put in charge of the inner treasury by the Late Emperor. After the present Emperor's accession he enjoyed exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye, the empress dowager's brother, had managed the inner treasury under the late emperor. The new emperor favored him above all others.

sentences.zh: 會宣徽使闕，業意欲之，帝及太后亦諷執政；

translations.literal: When the post of Palace Attendant became vacant, Ye wanted it. The Emperor and Empress Dowager also hinted this to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of palace attendant fell vacant, Li Ye wanted it—and emperor and empress dowager both signaled their wish to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 邠、弘肇以為內使遷補有次，不可以外戚超居，乃止。

translations.literal: Bin and Hongzhao held that inner-office promotions followed seniority and a maternal relative could not leap ahead. They blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao held that inner-office rank had its order and no maternal kinsman could jump the queue. They refused.

sentences.zh: 內客省使閻晉卿次當為宣徽使，久而不補。

translations.literal: Inner Guest Bureau Commissioner Yan Jinqing was next in line for Palace Attendant, but the post went unfilled for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jinqing of the Inner Guest Bureau stood next in line for palace attendant, yet the appointment lingered unfilled.

sentences.zh: 樞密承旨聶文進、飛龍使後匡贊、翰林茶酒使郭允明皆有寵於帝，久不遷官，共怨執政。

translations.literal: Privy Council Recipient Nie Wenjin, Flying Dragon Commissioner Hou Kuangzan, and Hanlin Tea and Wine Commissioner Guo Yunming all enjoyed the Emperor's favor yet long went without promotion. Together they resented the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Wenjin of the privy council, Hou Kuangzan of the Flying Dragon office, and Guo Yunming of the Hanlin tea and wine service all had the emperor's ear—and all languished without promotion. They hated the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 文進，并州人也。

translations.literal: Wenjin was a man of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Wenjin was from Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉銖罷青州歸，久奉朝請，未除官，常戟手於執政。

translations.literal: After Liu Zhu was dismissed from Qingzhou and returned, he attended court for a long time without receiving a post. He often shook his fist at the chief ministers in their presence.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhu, dismissed from Qingzhou, waited at court month after month without appointment. He shook his fist at the chief ministers to their faces.

sentences.zh: 帝初除三年喪，聽樂，賜伶人錦袍、玉帶。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first ended his three-year mourning and permitted music, he bestowed brocade robes and jade belts on the performers.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended and music returned to court, the emperor gave the players brocade robes and jade belts.

sentences.zh: 伶人詣弘肇謝，弘肇怒曰：「士卒守邊苦戰，猶未有以賜之，汝曹何功而得此！」

translations.literal: The performers went to thank Hongzhao. Hongzhao angrily said: "Frontier soldiers endure hardship and battle yet have received nothing like this—what merit have you to deserve it!"
translations.idiomatic: The players went to thank Shi Hongzhao. He exploded: "Soldiers on the frontier bleed in battle and get nothing like this. What have you done to deserve it?"

sentences.zh: 皆奪以還官。

translations.literal: He seized everything back for the government.
translations.idiomatic: He confiscated every gift and returned it to the state.

sentences.zh: 帝欲立所幸耿夫人為後，邠以為太速。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to install his favorite, Lady Geng, as empress. Bin thought it too soon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to make his favorite, Lady Geng, empress. Yang Bin said it was too soon.

sentences.zh: 夫人卒，帝欲以後禮葬之，邠復以為不可。

translations.literal: When the lady died, the Emperor wished to bury her with empress rites. Bin again objected.
translations.idiomatic: When she died, the emperor wanted empress rites for her burial. Yang Bin objected again.

sentences.zh: 帝年益壯，厭為大臣所制。

translations.literal: As the Emperor grew older, he wearied of being controlled by his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came of age and chafed under ministerial restraint.

sentences.zh: 邠、弘肇嘗議事於帝前，帝曰：「審圖之，勿令人有言！」

translations.literal: Bin and Hongzhao once deliberated before the Emperor. The Emperor said: "Think it through carefully—don't let people talk!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao debated policy before him, the emperor said, "Think it through—and don't give people cause to talk."

sentences.zh: 邠曰：「陛下但禁聲，有臣等在。」

translations.literal: Bin said: "Your Majesty need only forbid loose talk. We are here."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin replied, "Your Majesty need only silence gossip. We are here."

sentences.zh: 帝積不能平，左右因乘間譖之於帝云：「邠等專恣，終當為亂。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's resentment built without outlet. His attendants seized the moment to slander them: "Bin and the others are wilful and will eventually rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Resentment festered. The emperor's intimates whispered: "Yang Bin and his circle are arrogant—they will rebel in the end."

sentences.zh: 帝信之。

translations.literal: The Emperor believed them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed it.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜聞作坊鍛聲，疑有急兵，達旦不寐。

translations.literal: One night he heard hammering from the workshops and suspected troops were being rushed. He did not sleep until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: One night he heard the workshops hammering and imagined an army being forged. He lay awake until dawn.

sentences.zh: 司空、同平章事蘇逢吉既與弘肇有隙，知李業等怨弘肇，屢以言激之。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Su Fengji was already at odds with Hongzhao. Knowing that Li Ye and the others hated Hongzhao, he repeatedly goaded them with his words.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji, chief councilor, already hated Shi Hongzhao. Knowing that Li Ye and the rest despised him too, Su goaded them at every turn.

sentences.zh: 帝遂與業、文進、匡贊、允明謀誅邠等，議既定，入白太后。

translations.literal: The Emperor then plotted with Ye, Wenjin, Kuangzan, and Yunming to kill Bin and the others. Once the plan was set, he went to inform the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor plotted with Li Ye, Nie Wenjin, Hou Kuangzan, and Guo Yunming to kill Yang Bin and his colleagues. When the plan was fixed, he told the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「茲事何可輕發！

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "How can such a thing be lightly undertaken!
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "You cannot do a thing like this lightly!

sentences.zh: 更宜與宰相議之。」

translations.literal: You should discuss it further with the chief councilors."
translations.idiomatic: Talk it over with the chief councilors first."

sentences.zh: 業時在旁，曰：「先帝嘗言，朝廷大事不可謀及書生，懦怯誤人。」

translations.literal: Ye, who was nearby, said: "The Late Emperor once said that great matters of state must not be planned with bookish men—their timidity ruins everything."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye, standing by, said, "The late emperor warned that great affairs must never be entrusted to bookish men—their cowardice ruins everything."

sentences.zh: 太后復以為言，帝忿曰：「國家之事，非閨門所知！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager spoke again. The Emperor, furious, said: "Affairs of state are no business of the inner quarters!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager pressed her case. The emperor flared: "State affairs are no concern of the inner quarters!"

sentences.zh: 拂衣而出。

translations.literal: He shook out his robes and left.
translations.idiomatic: He swept out.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，業等以其謀告閻晉卿，晉卿恐事不成，詣弘肇第欲告之，弘肇以他故辭不見。

translations.literal: On yihai, Ye and the others told Yan Jinqing of their plot. Jinqing, fearing failure, went to Hongzhao's residence intending to report it, but Hongzhao declined to see him on some pretext.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Li Ye and the others confided the plot to Yan Jinqing. Fearful it would fail, Jinqing went to Shi Hongzhao's house to warn him—but Hongzhao refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 丙子旦，邠等入朝，有甲士數十自廣政殿出，殺邠、弘肇、章於東廡下。

translations.literal: At dawn on bingzi, Bin and the others entered court. Several dozen armored men emerged from the Guangzheng Hall and killed Bin, Hongzhao, and Zhang beneath the east gallery.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on bingzi, Yang Bin and his colleagues entered court. Dozens of armored men poured from the Guangzheng Hall and cut down Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and Wang Zhang under the east gallery.

sentences.zh: 文進亟召宰相、朝臣班於崇元殿，宣云：「邠等謀反，已伏誅，與卿等同慶！」

translations.literal: Wenjin hurriedly summoned the chief councilors and court officials to assemble at the Chongyuan Hall and announced: "Bin and the others plotted rebellion and have already been executed. Rejoice with us!"
translations.idiomatic: Nie Wenjin rushed the chief councilors and court officials to the Chongyuan Hall and proclaimed: "Yang Bin and the others plotted rebellion and are dead. Rejoice with us!"

sentences.zh: 又召諸軍將校至萬歲殿庭，帝親諭之，且曰：「邠等以稚子視朕，朕今始得為汝主，汝輩免橫憂矣！」

translations.literal: He also summoned army officers to the courtyard of the Wansui Hall. The Emperor addressed them in person and said: "Bin and the others treated me as a child. Now at last I am truly your lord—you are free from their tyranny!"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the army officers to the Wansui Hall courtyard. The emperor addressed them: "Yang Bin and his circle treated me as a child. Now I am truly your master—you are free of their oppression!"

sentences.zh: 皆拜謝而退。

translations.literal: All bowed in thanks and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed, thanked him, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又召前節度使、刺史等升殿諭之，分遣使者帥騎收捕邠等親戚、黨與、傔從，盡殺之。

translations.literal: He also summoned former military governors and prefects to the hall to address them, then dispatched envoys at the head of cavalry to seize and kill all relatives, associates, and retainers of Bin and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Former governors and prefects were summoned and addressed. Then cavalry envoys fanned out to seize and slaughter every relative, ally, and retainer of the dead ministers.

sentences.zh: 弘肇待侍衛步軍都指揮使王殷尤厚，邠等死，帝遣供奉官孟業繼密詔詣澶州及鄴都，令鎮寧節度使李洪義殺殷，又令鄴都行營馬軍都指揮使郭崇威、步軍都指揮使真定曹威殺郭威及監軍、宣徽使王峻。

translations.literal: Hongzhao had treated Palace Attendant Infantry Commander Wang Yin with particular kindness. After Bin and the others died, the Emperor sent Palace Attendant Meng Ye with secret orders to Danzhou and Yedu, ordering Zhenning Military Governor Li Hongyi to kill Yin, and ordering Yedu Campaign Cavalry Commander Guo Chongwei and Infantry Commander Cao Wei of Zhending to kill Guo Wei and the army inspector, Palace Attendant Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao had favored Wang Yin, infantry commander of the palace guard. After the killings the emperor sent Meng Ye with secret orders to Danzhou and Yedu: Li Hongyi of Zhenning was to kill Wang Yin; Guo Chongwei and Cao Wei of Zhending were to kill Guo Wei and the army inspector Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 洪義，太后之弟也。

translations.literal: Hongyi was the Empress Dowager's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongyi was the empress dowager's brother.

sentences.zh: 又急詔征天平軍節度使高行周、平盧節度使符彥卿、永興節度使郭從義、泰寧節度使慕容彥超、匡國節度使薛懷讓、鄭州防禦使吳虔裕、陳州刺史李穀入朝。

translations.literal: Urgent orders also summoned Tiance Military Governor Gao Xingzhou, Pinglu Military Governor Fu Yanqing, Yongxing Military Governor Guo Congyi, Taining Military Governor Murong Yanchao, Kuangguo Military Governor Xue Huairang, Zhengzhou Defense Commissioner Wu Qianyu, and Chenzhou Prefect Li Gu to court.
translations.idiomatic: Urgent summons went out to Gao Xingzhou of Tiance, Fu Yanqing of Pinglu, Guo Congyi of Yongxing, Murong Yanchao of Taining, Xue Huairang of Kuangguo, Wu Qianyu of Zhengzhou, and Li Gu of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 以蘇逢吉權知樞密院事，前平盧節度使劉銖權知開封府，侍衛馬軍都指揮使李洪建權判侍衛同事，內侍省使閻晉卿權侍衛馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Su Fengji was made acting Privy Council Director; former Pinglu Military Governor Liu Zhu acting Kaifeng Administrator; Palace Attendant Cavalry Commander Li Hongjian acting Palace Attendant concurrent administrator; Inner Service Commissioner Yan Jinqing acting Palace Attendant Cavalry Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji took the privy council in trust; Liu Zhu, former governor of Pinglu, took Kaifeng; Li Hongjian, cavalry commander, took concurrent charge of the palace guard; Yan Jinqing took the cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 洪建，業之兄也。

translations.literal: Hongjian was Ye's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongjian was Li Ye's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 時中外人情憂駭，蘇逢吉雖惡弘肇，而不預李業等謀，聞變驚愕，私謂人曰：「事太匆匆，主上倘以一言見問，不至於此。」

translations.literal: At the time people inside and outside the court were stricken with dread. Though Su Fengji hated Hongzhao, he had not joined Li Ye's plot. When he heard what had happened he was appalled and said privately: "This was far too hasty. If the Emperor had asked me a single question, it would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Terror gripped the court and the city. Su Fengji had hated Shi Hongzhao but had not joined the plot. When he heard the news he was stunned. "Too hasty," he said privately. "One word from the emperor and this need not have happened."

sentences.zh: 業等命劉銖誅郭威、王峻之家，銖極其慘毒，嬰孺無免者。

translations.literal: Ye and the others ordered Liu Zhu to exterminate the families of Guo Wei and Wang Jun. Zhu was monstrously cruel—not even infants were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye ordered Liu Zhu to wipe out the families of Guo Wei and Wang Jun. Zhu was savage—not even infants were spared.

sentences.zh: 命李洪建誅王殷之家，洪建但使人守視，仍飲食之。

translations.literal: They ordered Li Hongjian to exterminate Wang Yin's family. Hongjian merely posted guards to watch over them and continued to provide food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongjian was told to destroy Wang Yin's household. He posted guards, watched over them, and kept them fed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，使者至澶州，李洪義畏懦，慮王殷已知其事，不敢發，乃引孟業見殷。

translations.literal: On dingchou the envoys reached Danzhou. Li Hongyi, cowardly and fearful, worried that Wang Yin already knew the plan and dared not act. He brought Meng Ye to see Yin.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the envoys reached Danzhou. Li Hongyi, craven and afraid Wang Yin already knew, dared not strike. He brought Meng Ye before Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷囚業，遣副使陳光穗以密詔示郭威。

translations.literal: Yin imprisoned Ye and sent Deputy Commissioner Chen Guangsu to show the secret order to Guo Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin jailed Meng Ye and sent his deputy Chen Guangsu to show the secret order to Guo Wei.

sentences.zh: 威召樞密吏魏仁浦，示以詔書曰：「奈何？」

translations.literal: Wei summoned Privy Council clerk Wei Renpu, showed him the edict, and said: "What am I to do?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei called Wei Renpu, his privy council clerk, showed him the edict, and asked, "What now?"

sentences.zh: 仁浦曰：「公，國之大臣，功名素著，加之握強兵，據重鎮，一旦為群小所構，禍出非意，此非辭說所能解。

translations.literal: Renpu said: "You are a great minister of the state, renowned for achievement, and besides you command strong troops and hold a vital post. To be framed by petty men and meet disaster you never expected—no words can undo that.
translations.idiomatic: Renpu said, "You are a pillar of the state, famous for your deeds, commanding strong troops from a vital post. Petty men have framed you for a death you never earned. No plea will save you.

sentences.zh: 時事如此，不可坐而待死。」

translations.literal: Matters stand thus. You cannot sit and wait for death."
translations.idiomatic: Matters stand as they stand. You cannot sit and wait to die."

sentences.zh: 威乃召郭崇威、曹威及諸將，告以楊邠等冤死及有密詔之狀，且曰：「吾與諸公，披荊棘，從先帝取天下，受托孤之任，竭力以衛國家，今諸公已死，吾何心獨生！

translations.literal: Wei then summoned Guo Chongwei, Cao Wei, and the other generals, told them of the wrongful deaths of Yang Bin and the others and of the secret order, and said: "You and I carved through thorns and followed the Late Emperor to win the empire. We accepted the charge of guarding the orphan and strained every nerve to defend the state. Now you are dead—what heart have I to live alone!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei gathered Guo Chongwei, Cao Wei, and the other generals, told them how Yang Bin and the rest had been murdered and showed them the secret order. "We cut through thorns beside the late emperor and won this empire," he said. "We took the orphan in trust and gave everything to defend the realm. You are dead—how can I live alone?

sentences.zh: 君輩當奉行詔書，取吾首以報天子，庶不相累。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen should carry out the edict, take my head to report to the Son of Heaven, so you may not be dragged down with me."
translations.idiomatic: Carry out the edict. Take my head to the emperor so you are not destroyed with me."

sentences.zh: 郭崇威等皆泣曰：「天子幼沖，此必左右群小所為，若使此輩得志，國家其得安乎！

translations.literal: Guo Chongwei and the others wept and said: "The Son of Heaven is still young—this must be the work of petty men around the throne. If such men prevail, how can the state know peace!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongwei and the others wept. "The emperor is young—this is the work of rats at his ear. If they win, the realm is lost!

sentences.zh: 崇威願從公入朝自訴，蕩滌鼠輩以清朝廷，不可為單使所殺，受千載惡名。」

translations.literal: Chongwei is willing to follow you to court to plead our case, sweep away these rats and cleanse the court. We cannot let a lone envoy cut you down and earn infamy for a thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: I will follow you to court, drive out these vermin, and cleanse the palace. We will not let a lone envoy cut you down and leave our names in infamy for a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 翰林天文趙修已謂郭威曰：「公徒死何益！

translations.literal: Hanlin Astronomer Zhao Xiu already told Guo Wei: "What good is dying for nothing!
translations.idiomatic: The Hanlin astronomer Zhao Xiu had already told Guo Wei, "What good is a useless death?

sentences.zh: 不若順眾心，擁兵而南，此天啟也。」

translations.literal: Better obey the will of the masses, take up arms, and march south—this is Heaven's opening."
translations.idiomatic: Better follow the army's will, take up arms, and march south. Heaven itself opens the way."

sentences.zh: 郭威乃留其養子榮鎮鄴都，命郭崇威將騎兵前驅，戊寅，自將大軍繼之。

translations.literal: Guo Wei left his adopted son Rong to hold Yedu, ordered Guo Chongwei to lead the cavalry vanguard, and on wuyin personally followed with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei left his adopted son Rong at Yedu, sent Guo Chongwei ahead with the cavalry, and on wuyin marched south at the head of the main force.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超方食，得詔，捨匕箸入朝。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao was at his meal when the edict arrived. He set down chopsticks and entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao was at table when the summons came. He laid down his chopsticks and went to court.

sentences.zh: 帝悉以軍事委之。

translations.literal: The Emperor entrusted all military affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him full command.

sentences.zh: 己卯，吳虔裕入朝。

translations.literal: On jimao, Wu Qianyu entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Wu Qianyu arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 帝聞郭威舉兵南向，議發兵拒之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard that Guo Wei had raised troops marching south, he deliberated sending troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Guo Wei was marching south with an army, the emperor debated sending forces to stop him.

sentences.zh: 前開封尹侯益曰：「鄴都戍兵家屬皆在京師，官軍不可輕出，不若閉城以挫其鋒，使其母妻登城招之，可不戰而下也。」

translations.literal: Former Kaifeng Administrator Hou Yi said: "The garrison families of Yedu all live in the capital. The imperial army must not march out lightly. Better shut the city to blunt their edge and let their mothers and wives climb the walls to call them back—they may submit without battle."
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi, former administrator of Kaifeng, said, "Every Yedu soldier's family is in the capital. Do not march out. Shut the gates, break their momentum, and let their mothers and wives call from the walls—they may yield without a fight."

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超曰：「侯益衰老，為懦夫計耳。」

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao said: "Hou Yi is old and feeble—this is a coward's plan."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao said, "Hou Yi is old and broken—that is a coward's counsel."

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣益及閻晉卿、吳虔裕、前保大節度使張彥超將禁軍趣澶州。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent Yi along with Yan Jinqing, Wu Qianyu, and former Baoda Military Governor Zhang Yanchao to lead the palace guard toward Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Hou Yi, Yan Jinqing, Wu Qianyu, and Zhang Yanchao, former governor of Baoda, with the palace guard toward Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，郭威已至澶州，李洪義納之。

translations.literal: That same day Guo Wei had already reached Danzhou. Li Hongyi admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Guo Wei was already at Danzhou. Li Hongyi opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 王殷迎謁慟哭，以所部兵從郭威涉河。

translations.literal: Wang Yin came out to greet him weeping, and with his troops followed Guo Wei across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin came out weeping to meet him and crossed the river with his troops behind Guo Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝遣內養鸗脫覘郭威，威獲之，以表置鸗脫衣領中，使歸白帝曰：「臣昨得詔書，延頸俟死。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent inner attendant Ying Tuo to spy on Guo Wei. Wei captured him, placed his memorial inside Ying Tuo's collar, and sent him back to tell the Emperor: "Yesterday I received the edict and stretched my neck awaiting death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the inner attendant Ying Tuo to spy on Guo Wei. Guo Wei seized him, tucked a memorial into his collar, and sent him back with a message: "Yesterday I received the edict and offered my neck for the blade.

sentences.zh: 郭崇威等不忍殺臣，雲此皆陛下左右貪權無厭者譖臣耳，逼臣南行，詣闕請罪。

translations.literal: Guo Chongwei and the others could not bear to kill me. They say this is all slander from your Majesty's greedy, power-hungry attendants—it forced me south to come to court and plead guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongwei and the others could not bear to kill me. They say your greedy attendants slandered me and forced me south to plead at court.

sentences.zh: 臣求死不獲，力不能制。

translations.literal: I sought death and could not obtain it. I lack the strength to resist.
translations.idiomatic: I sought death and was denied. I have not the power to resist.

sentences.zh: 臣數日當至闕庭。

translations.literal: In a few days I shall reach the court.
translations.idiomatic: In a few days I will stand before the throne.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以臣為有罪，安敢逃刑！

translations.literal: If your Majesty holds me guilty, how dare I flee punishment!
translations.idiomatic: If I am guilty, I will not flee punishment!

sentences.zh: 若實有譖臣者，願執付軍前以快眾心，臣敢不撫諭諸軍，退歸鄴都！」

translations.literal: If there are truly those who slandered me, I ask that they be handed over at the front to satisfy the army. I dare promise to calm the troops and withdraw to Yedu!"
translations.idiomatic: If I was slandered, hand the slanderers to the army and I will calm the troops and withdraw to Yedu!"

sentences.zh: 庚辰，郭威趣滑州。

translations.literal: On gengchen Guo Wei pressed toward Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Guo Wei marched on Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，義成節度使宋延渥迎降。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Yicheng Military Governor Song Yanwo came out to welcome him and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Song Yanwo of Yicheng came out to welcome him and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 延渥，洛陽人，其妻晉高祖女永寧公主也。

translations.literal: Yanwo was a Luoyang man; his wife was Princess Yongning, daughter of the Late Jin Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yanwo was from Luoyang; his wife was Princess Yongning, daughter of the late Jin emperor Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 郭威取滑州庫物以勞將士，且諭之曰：「聞侯令公已督諸軍自南來，今遇之，交戰則非入朝之義，不戰則為其所屬。

translations.literal: Guo Wei took goods from Huazhou's storehouses to reward the troops and addressed them: "I hear Commander Hou has already driven the armies south from the capital. If we meet in battle that is not the meaning of entering court. If we do not fight we fall under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei opened Huazhou's stores to reward the army and told them, "Hou Yi is driving the imperial forces south. Battle would betray the purpose of this march; refusal would put us under his command.

sentences.zh: 吾欲全汝曹功名，不若奉行前詔，吾死不恨！」

translations.literal: I wish to preserve your merit and fame. Better to carry out the earlier edict—I shall not regret death!"
translations.idiomatic: I would save your honor. Better execute the old order—I will not regret dying!"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「國家負公，公不負國，所以萬人爭奮。
