translations.literal: All said: "The state wronged you; you did not wrong the state—that is why ten thousand men strive forward.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The state wronged you; you did not wrong the state. That is why ten thousand men press forward.

sentences.zh: 如報私仇，侯益輩何能為乎！」

translations.literal: If this is private vengeance, what can Hou Yi and his ilk accomplish!"
translations.idiomatic: If this is vengeance, what can Hou Yi and his sort do?"

sentences.zh: 王峻徇於眾曰：「我得公處分，俟克京城，聽旬日剽掠。」

translations.literal: Wang Jun proclaimed to the masses: "By the General's order, once we take the capital you may plunder for ten days."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun cried through the ranks, "By the general's order—ten days of plunder once we take the capital!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆踴躍。

translations.literal: The troops leaped with eagerness.
translations.idiomatic: The men roared with eagerness.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，鸗脫至大梁。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Ying Tuo reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Ying Tuo reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 前此帝議自往澶州，聞郭威已至河上而止。

translations.literal: Earlier the Emperor had deliberated going personally to Danzhou, but stopped when he heard Guo Wei had reached the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had considered going to Danzhou himself, but halted when he learned Guo Wei had reached the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 帝甚有悔懼之色，私謂竇貞固曰：「屬者亦太草草。」

translations.literal: The Emperor looked deeply repentant and afraid. He said privately to Dou Zhengu: "This was handled far too rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Fear and regret showed on his face. To Dou Zhengu he whispered, "We moved too rashly."

sentences.zh: 李業等請傾府庫以賜諸軍，蘇禹珪以為未可，業拜禹珪於帝前，曰：「相公且為天子勿惜府庫！」

translations.literal: Li Ye and the others asked to empty the treasury to reward the armies. Su Yugui thought it inadvisable. Ye bowed to Yugui before the Emperor and said: "Chancellor, spare the treasury for the Son of Heaven's sake!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye demanded the treasury be emptied to pay the army. Su Yugui objected. Li Ye bowed to him before the emperor: "Chancellor—for the emperor's sake, do not hoard the vault!"

sentences.zh: 乃賜禁軍人二十緡，下軍半之，將士在北者給其家，仍使通家信以誘之。

translations.literal: They then gave twenty strings of cash per palace guard soldier, half that to lower ranks; those fighting in the north had rations sent to their families, and family letters were allowed through to entice them.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards received twenty strings of cash each, lesser ranks half that. Families of northern troops got rations; letters from home were allowed through to turn them.

sentences.zh: 壬午，郭威軍至封丘，人情忷懼。

translations.literal: On renwu Guo Wei's army reached Fengqiu. Public feeling was deeply alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Guo Wei reached Fengqiu. Dread spread through the city.

sentences.zh: 太后泣曰：「不用李濤之言，宜其亡也！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager wept: "Had we heeded Li Tao's counsel, this would not have happened!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wept, "Had we listened to Li Tao, none of this would have come!"

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超恃其驍勇，言於帝曰：「臣視北軍猶蠛蠓耳，當為陛下生致其魁！」

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao, trusting in his fierce courage, told the Emperor: "I regard the northern army as no more than gnats—I shall capture their leader alive for your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao, sure of his own ferocity, told the emperor, "The northern army is gnats to me. I will bring you their leader alive!"

sentences.zh: 退，見聶文進，問北來兵數及將校姓名，頗懼，曰：「是亦劇賊，未易輕也！」

translations.literal: When he withdrew he saw Nie Wenjin, asked the numbers of the northern troops and their commanders' names, grew quite afraid, and said: "These too are formidable bandits—not to be taken lightly!"
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawn, he asked Nie Wenjin how many northerners were coming and who led them. His bravado collapsed. "Hard fighters," he said. "Not to be taken lightly."

sentences.zh: 帝復遣左神武統軍袁㠖、前威勝節度使劉重進等帥禁軍與侯益等會屯赤岡。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Left Spirit Martial Commander Yuan Qiang, former Weisheng Military Governor Liu Chongjin, and others to lead the palace guard to join Hou Yi and encamp at Chigang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yuan Qiang of the Left Spirit Martial Guard, Liu Chongjin of Weisheng, and others with the palace guard to join Hou Yi at Chigang.

sentences.zh: 㠖，像先之子也。

translations.literal: Qiang was the son of Xiangxian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qiang was the son of Xiangxian.

sentences.zh: 彥超以大軍屯七里店。

translations.literal: Yanchao encamped the main army at Qilidian.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao camped the main force at Qilidian.

sentences.zh: 癸未，南、北軍遇於劉子陂。

translations.literal: On guimwei the southern and northern armies met at Liuzipo.
translations.idiomatic: On guimwei the southern and northern armies faced each other at Liuzipo.

sentences.zh: 帝欲自出勞軍，太后曰：「郭威吾家故舊，非死亡切身，何以至此！

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to go out personally to encourage the troops. The Empress Dowager said: "Guo Wei is an old friend of our house. Unless death itself pressed upon him, why would he come to this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to ride out and rally the troops. The empress dowager said, "Guo Wei is an old friend of our house. Only mortal peril would bring him to this!

sentences.zh: 但按兵守城，飛詔諭之，觀其志趣，必有辭理，則君臣之禮尚全，慎勿輕出。」

translations.literal: Simply hold the army and defend the city. Dispatch urgent edicts to instruct him and observe his intent—there must be grounds for explanation, and the rites between lord and subject may yet remain intact. Do not go out lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Hold the walls. Send urgent edicts, read his intent—there must be room to talk, and lord and subject may yet keep their forms. Do not go out lightly."

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時扈從軍甚盛，太后遣使戒聶文進曰：「大須在意！」

translations.literal: At the time the entourage army was very large. The Empress Dowager sent a messenger to warn Nie Wenjin: "You must take great care!"
translations.idiomatic: The imperial escort was huge. The empress dowager sent word to Nie Wenjin: "Take care!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「有臣在，雖郭威百人，可擒也！」

translations.literal: He replied: "With me here, even a hundred Guo Weis could be captured!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "With me here, a hundred Guo Weis could be taken!"

sentences.zh: 至暮，兩軍不戰，帝還宮。

translations.literal: By evening the two armies had not fought. The Emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: By evening neither side had struck. The emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超大言曰：「陛下來日宮中無事，幸再出觀臣破賊。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao boasted loudly: "Your Majesty need not concern yourself tomorrow—the court will be untroubled. Pray come out again to watch me break the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao boasted, "Tomorrow the palace will be untroubled, Majesty. Come watch me break the rebels.

sentences.zh: 臣不必與之戰，但叱散使歸營耳！」

translations.literal: I need not even fight them—only shout them apart and send them back to camp!"
translations.idiomatic: I need not even fight—I will shout them apart and send them back to camp!"

sentences.zh: 甲申，帝欲再出，太后力止之，不可。

translations.literal: On jiashen the Emperor wished to go out again. The Empress Dowager tried hard to stop him but could not.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the emperor wanted to ride out again. The empress dowager fought to stop him and failed.

sentences.zh: 既陳，郭威戒其眾曰：「吾來誅群小，非敢敵天子也，慎勿先動。」

translations.literal: Once the armies were drawn up, Guo Wei warned his men: "I come to execute petty men, not to oppose the Son of Heaven. Take care—do not strike first."
translations.idiomatic: When the lines were set, Guo Wei warned his men, "I come to kill the rats at court, not to fight the emperor. Do not strike first."

sentences.zh: 久之，慕容彥超引輕騎直前奮擊，郭崇威與前博州刺史李榮帥騎兵拒之。

translations.literal: After a long while Murong Yanchao led light cavalry straight forward in a fierce charge. Guo Chongwei and former Bozhou Prefect Li Rong led cavalry to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: After a long standoff Murong Yanchao charged with light cavalry. Guo Chongwei and Li Rong of Bozhou met him with horse.

sentences.zh: 彥超馬倒，幾獲之。

translations.literal: Yanchao's horse fell; he was nearly captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao's horse went down. He was nearly taken.

sentences.zh: 彥超引兵退，麾下死者百餘人，於是諸軍奪氣，稍稍降於北軍。

translations.literal: Yanchao withdrew. More than a hundred of his followers died. At that the various armies lost heart and gradually surrendered to the northern army.
translations.idiomatic: He pulled back with more than a hundred dead. Heart went out of the southern ranks; one by one they went over to the north.

sentences.zh: 侯益、吳虔裕、張彥超、袁㠖、劉重進皆潛往見郭威，威各遣還營，又謂宋延渥曰：「天子方危，公近親，宜以牙兵往衛乘輿，且附奏陛下，願乘間早幸臣營。」

translations.literal: Hou Yi, Wu Qianyu, Zhang Yanchao, Yuan Qiang, and Liu Chongjin all stole away to see Guo Wei. Wei sent each back to camp, and also told Song Yanwo: "The Son of Heaven is in peril. You are a close kinsman—take your guards to protect the imperial carriage, and send a memorial saying you hope your Majesty will soon visit my camp when opportunity permits."
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi, Wu Qianyu, Zhang Yanchao, Yuan Qiang, and Liu Chongjin slipped away to Guo Wei. He sent each back to camp and told Song Yanwo, "The emperor is in danger. You are kin—take your guard to the imperial carriage and ask that his Majesty come to my camp when he can."

sentences.zh: 延渥未至御營，亂兵雲擾，不敢進而還。

translations.literal: Before Yanwo reached the imperial camp, disorderly troops swarmed like clouds. He dared not advance and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Before Song Yanwo reached the imperial camp, chaos swarmed like clouds. He dared not go on and turned back.

sentences.zh: 比暮，南軍多歸於北。

translations.literal: By evening most of the southern army had gone over to the north.
translations.idiomatic: By evening the southern army had mostly gone north.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超與麾下十餘騎奔還兗州。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao fled back to Yanzhou with little more than ten followers.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao fled to Yanzhou with a dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝獨與三相及從官數十人宿於七里寨，餘皆逃潰。

translations.literal: That night the Emperor alone, with the three chief councilors and several dozen attendants, slept at the Qili stockade. All the rest fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor slept at the Qili stockade with only the three chief councilors and a few dozen attendants. Everyone else ran.

sentences.zh: 乙酉旦，郭威望見天子旌旗在高阪上，下馬免冑往從之，至則帝已去矣。

translations.literal: At dawn on yiyou Guo Wei saw the Son of Heaven's banners on a high slope. He dismounted, removed his helmet, and went toward them—but when he arrived the Emperor was already gone.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on yiyou Guo Wei saw the imperial banners on a rise. He dismounted, bared his head, and went to them—but the emperor was already gone.

sentences.zh: 帝策馬將還宮，至玄化門，劉銖在門上，問帝左右：「兵馬何在？」

translations.literal: The Emperor spurred his horse intending to return to the palace. At the Xuanhua Gate Liu Zhu was on the gate tower and asked the Emperor's attendants: "Where are the troops?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wheeled toward the palace. At the Xuanhua Gate Liu Zhu stood on the tower and called down, "Where is your army?"

sentences.zh: 因射左右。

translations.literal: Then he shot at the attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Then he shot at the emperor's men.

sentences.zh: 帝回轡，西北至趙村，追兵已至，帝下馬入民家，為亂兵所弒。

translations.literal: The Emperor wheeled his horse northwest to Zhaocun. Pursuers arrived. He dismounted and entered a commoner's house, where mutinous soldiers killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned northwest to Zhaocun. Pursuers caught him. He dismounted and hid in a peasant's house. Mutinous soldiers killed him there.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉、閻晉卿、郭允明皆自殺。

translations.literal: Su Fengji, Yan Jinqing, and Guo Yunming all killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji, Yan Jinqing, and Guo Yunming took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 聶文進挺身走，軍士追趕斬之。

translations.literal: Nie Wenjin fled on foot. Soldiers pursued and cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Wenjin ran on foot. Soldiers chased him down and killed him.

sentences.zh: 李業奔陝州，後匡贊奔兗州。

translations.literal: Li Ye fled to Shanzhou; Hou Kuangzan fled to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye fled to Shanzhou; Hou Kuangzan to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 郭威聞帝遇弒，號慟曰：「老夫之罪也！」

translations.literal: When Guo Wei heard the Emperor had been murdered he wailed: "This old man's crime!"
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei heard the emperor was dead he wailed, "This old man's crime!"

sentences.zh: 威至玄化門，劉銖雨射城外。

translations.literal: When Wei reached the Xuanhua Gate, Liu Zhu rained arrows outside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuanhua Gate Liu Zhu showered arrows from the wall.

sentences.zh: 威自迎春門入，歸私第，遣前曹州防禦使何福進將兵守明德門。

translations.literal: Wei entered through the Yingchun Gate, returned to his private residence, and sent former Caozhou Defense Commissioner He Fujin to hold the Mingde Gate with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei entered by the Yingchun Gate, went to his own house, and sent He Fujin of Caozhou to hold the Mingde Gate.

sentences.zh: 諸軍大掠，通夕煙火四發。

translations.literal: The armies plundered on a vast scale. All night fires rose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: The army looted without restraint. Fires burned on every side through the night.

sentences.zh: 軍士入前義成節度使白再榮之第，執再榮，盡掠其財，既而進曰：「某等昔嘗趨走麾下，一旦無禮至此，何面目復見公！」

translations.literal: Soldiers entered the residence of former Yicheng Military Governor Bai Zairong, seized Zairong, and stripped him of all his wealth. Then one stepped forward and said: "We once ran errands under your command—yet now we have treated you with such disrespect. What face have we to see you again!"
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers broke into the house of Bai Zairong, former governor of Yicheng, seized him, and stripped him bare. One said, "We once served under you—and now we have shamed you. What face have we to meet yours?"

sentences.zh: 遂刎其首而去。

translations.literal: Then they cut off his head and left.
translations.idiomatic: They cut off his head and went.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎張允，家貲以萬計，而性吝，雖妻亦不之委，常自系眾鑰於衣下，行如環珮。

translations.literal: Ministry of Personnel Vice Director Zhang Yun's household wealth ran to tens of thousands, yet he was miserly by nature. Even his wife he would not trust with it. He always tied a bundle of keys beneath his clothes, jingling like jade pendants as he walked.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun of the Ministry of Personnel was worth tens of thousands yet could not spend a coin. He trusted not even his wife. He wore all his keys beneath his robe, clinking like jade as he walked.

sentences.zh: 是夕，匿於佛殿藻井之上，登者浸多，板壞而墜，軍士掠其衣，遂以凍卒。

translations.literal: That night he hid in the coffered ceiling of a Buddhist hall. As more climbed up the boards broke and he fell. Soldiers stripped his clothes and he froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: That night he hid in the rafters of a temple hall. Others climbed up; the beams gave way and he fell. Soldiers took his clothes. He froze to death.

sentences.zh: 初，作坊使賈延徽有寵於帝，與魏仁浦為鄰，欲並仁浦所居以自廣，屢譖仁浦於帝，幾至不測。

translations.literal: Earlier, Workshop Commissioner Jia Yanhui had enjoyed the Emperor's favor. He was Guo Wei's neighbor and wanted to take over Renpu's residence to enlarge his own. He repeatedly slandered Renpu to the Emperor, nearly bringing him to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Once, Jia Yanhui of the workshops had the emperor's favor. Neighbor to Guo Wei, he wanted Wei Renpu's house for his own and slandered Renpu to the throne until disaster nearly found him.

sentences.zh: 至是，有擒延徽以授仁浦者，仁浦謝曰：「因亂而報怨，吾所不為也！」

translations.literal: Now someone seized Yanhui and delivered him to Renpu. Renpu declined: "To settle scores amid chaos—that I will not do!"
translations.idiomatic: Now men seized Yanhui and brought him to Renpu. Renpu refused: "I will not settle scores in chaos!"

sentences.zh: 郭威聞之，待仁浦益厚。

translations.literal: When Guo Wei heard of it he treated Renpu with even greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei heard and favored Renpu all the more.

sentences.zh: 右千牛衛大將軍棗強趙鳳曰：「郭侍中舉兵，欲誅君側之惡以安國家耳；

translations.literal: Right Thousand-Ox Gate General Zhao Feng of Zaoqiang said: "Attendant Guo raised troops intending to execute the evil at the Son of Heaven's side and secure the state—
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng of Zaoqiang, Right Thousand-Ox Gate general, said, "Attendant Guo marched to kill the evil beside the throne and save the realm—

sentences.zh: 而鼠輩敢爾，乃賊也，豈侍中意邪！」

translations.literal: yet these rats dared as much as this—they are bandits! Is this Attendant Guo's wish!"
translations.idiomatic: and these rats dare this? They are bandits! Is this what Attendant Guo wanted?"

sentences.zh: 執弓矢，踞胡床，坐於巷首，掠者至，輒射殺之，裡中皆賴以全。

translations.literal: He took bow and arrows, sat on a camp chair at the lane's head, and whenever plunderers came shot them dead. The neighborhood was preserved intact because of him.
translations.idiomatic: He took bow and arrow, sat on a camp stool at the lane mouth, and shot every looter who came. The neighborhood survived because of him.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，獲劉銖、李洪建，囚之。

translations.literal: On bingxu Liu Zhu and Li Hongjian were captured and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Liu Zhu and Li Hongjian were taken and jailed.

sentences.zh: 銖謂其妻曰：「我死，汝且為人婢乎？」

translations.literal: Zhu said to his wife: "When I die, will you become someone's servant girl?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhu told his wife, "When I die, will you be another man's servant?"

sentences.zh: 妻曰：「以公所為，雅當然耳！」

translations.literal: His wife said: "Given what you have done, it is only fitting!"
translations.idiomatic: His wife said, "Given what you have done, that is only fitting."

sentences.zh: 王殷、郭崇威言於郭威曰：「不止剽掠，今夕止有空城耳。」

translations.literal: Wang Yin and Guo Chongwei said to Guo Wei: "If we do not stop the looting, by tonight there will be nothing left but an empty city."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin and Guo Chongwei said to Guo Wei, "If we do not stop the looting, by tonight there will be nothing left but an empty city."

sentences.zh: 威乃命諸將分部禁止掠者，不從則斬之。

translations.literal: Guo Wei then ordered the generals to divide up and forbid looters; those who disobeyed were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei ordered his generals to divide the city and suppress looters; anyone who refused was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 至晡，乃定。

translations.literal: By late afternoon, order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon the city was calm again.

sentences.zh: 竇貞固、蘇禹珪自七里寨逃歸，郭威使人訪求得之，尋復其位。

translations.literal: Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui fled back from Qili Stockade; Guo Wei sent men to find them and soon restored them to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui fled back from Qili Stockade. Guo Wei had them tracked down and soon restored them to office.

sentences.zh: 貞固為相，值楊、史弄權，李業等作亂，但以凝重處其間，自全而已。

translations.literal: Zhengu had served as chancellor when Yang and Shi abused power and Li Ye raised rebellion; he had preserved himself by remaining grave and restrained among them—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengu had been chancellor while Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao manipulated power and Li Ye stirred rebellion; he had survived by holding himself aloof and grave—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 郭威命有司遷隱帝梓宮於西宮。

translations.literal: Guo Wei ordered the officials to move the Hidden Emperor's coffin to the Western Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei ordered the Hidden Emperor's coffin moved to the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 或請如魏高貴鄉公故事，葬以公禮。

translations.literal: Some proposed following the precedent of the Wei dynasty's Duke of Gaogui Township and burying him with ducal rites.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged that he be buried with ducal honors, as the Wei had done for the Duke of Gaogui Township.

sentences.zh: 威不許，曰：「倉猝之際，吾不能保衛乘輿，罪已大矣，況敢貶君乎！」

translations.literal: Guo Wei refused, saying: "In that desperate moment I could not protect the imperial carriage—my crime was already great enough; how could I dare further demean my sovereign?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei refused. "In that desperate hour I failed to protect the throne," he said. "My guilt was already great enough—how could I dare demean my sovereign further?"

sentences.zh: 太師馮道帥百官謁見郭威，威見，猶拜之，道受拜如平時，徐曰：「侍中此行不易！」

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Feng Dao led the officials to call on Guo Wei; when Guo Wei saw him he still bowed, and Feng accepted the bow as usual, saying slowly: "Your Excellency's journey here was no easy matter!"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Feng Dao led the officials to pay their respects to Guo Wei. Guo Wei still bowed to him; Feng received the bow as he always had and said quietly, "Your Excellency, this road you have walked was not an easy one."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，郭威帥百官詣明德門起居太后，且奏稱：「軍國事殷，請早立嗣君。」

translations.literal: On dinghai, Guo Wei led the officials to the Gate of Virtuous Clarity to pay respects to the Empress Dowager, and memorialized: "State and military affairs press urgently—please establish a successor soon."
translations.idiomatic: “On dinghai, Guo Wei led the officials to the Gate of Virtuous Clarity to attend the Empress Dowager and memorialized that state and military affairs were pressing and a successor should be enthroned without delay.”

sentences.zh: 太后誥稱：「郭允明弒逆，神器不可無主。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's decree read: "Guo Yunming committed regicide; the sacred vessel of rule cannot be without a master.
translations.idiomatic: “The Empress Dowager's decree declared that Guo Yunming had murdered his sovereign and that the throne could not remain empty.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使崇，忠武節度使信，皆高祖之弟；

translations.literal: Military Governor of Hedong, Chong, and Military Governor of Zhongwu, Xin—both are younger brothers of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, military governor of Hedong, and Xin, military governor of Zhongwu, were both younger brothers of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使贇，開封尹勳，高祖之子。

translations.literal: Military Governor of Wuning, Yun, and Mayor of Kaifeng, Xun—sons of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, military governor of Wuning, and Xun, mayor of Kaifeng, were sons of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 其令百官議擇所宜。」

translations.literal: Let the officials deliberate and choose whomever is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Let the officials meet and choose whoever is most suitable."

sentences.zh: 贇，崇之子也，高祖愛之，養視如子。

translations.literal: Yun was Chong's son; Gaozu loved him and raised him as his own.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was Chong's son, but Gaozu loved him and raised him as if he were his own.

sentences.zh: 郭威、王峻入見太后於萬歲宮，請以勳為嗣。

translations.literal: Guo Wei and Wang Jun entered the Palace of Ten Thousand Years to see the Empress Dowager and proposed Xun as successor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei and Wang Jun went to the Palace of Ten Thousand Years and asked the Empress Dowager to name Xun as heir.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「勳久贏疾不能起。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager said: "Xun has long been wasted by illness and cannot rise."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said, "Xun has long been crippled by illness and cannot even rise."

sentences.zh: 威出諭諸將，諸將請見之，太后令左右以臥榻舉之示諸將，諸將乃信之。

translations.literal: Guo Wei went out and informed the generals; they asked to see him, and the Empress Dowager had attendants lift his couch-bed to show the generals—they then believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei went out and told the generals. They asked to see Xun for themselves, and the Empress Dowager had attendants carry his sickbed forward so they could look—then they believed it.

sentences.zh: 於是郭威與峻議立贇。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guo Wei and Jun deliberated on installing Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei and Wang Jun then agreed to install Liu Yun instead.

sentences.zh: 己丑，郭威帥百官表請以贇承大統。

translations.literal: On jichou, Guo Wei led the officials in memorializing that Yun should succeed to the Great Line.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Guo Wei led the officials in petitioning that Liu Yun succeed to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太后誥所司，擇日，備法駕迎贇即皇帝位。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager decreed to the responsible offices to choose a day, prepare the imperial escort, and welcome Yun to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered the appropriate offices to fix a date, prepare the imperial escort, and bring Yun to the capital to be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 郭威奏遣太師馮道及樞密直學士王度、秘書監趙上交詣徐州奉迎。

translations.literal: Guo Wei memorialized sending Grand Preceptor Feng Dao, Hanlin Academician Wang Du, and Director of the Secretariat Zhao Shangjiao to Xuzhou to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei proposed sending Grand Preceptor Feng Dao, Hanlin academician Wang Du, and Secretariat director Zhao Shangjiao to Xuzhou to escort the new emperor west.

sentences.zh: 郭威之討三叛也，每見朝廷詔書，處分軍事皆合機宜，問使者：「誰為此詔？」

translations.literal: When Guo Wei was campaigning against the three rebellions, whenever he saw court edicts whose military dispositions all matched circumstances, he asked the messenger: "Who drafted this edict?"
translations.idiomatic: While Guo Wei was suppressing the three rebellions, he noticed that every court edict on military affairs was perfectly timed. He asked the messenger, "Who wrote these orders?"

sentences.zh: 使者以翰林學士范質對。

translations.literal: The messenger named Hanlin Academician Fan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger answered: Hanlin academician Fan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 威曰：「宰相器也。」

translations.literal: Guo Wei said: "Material for a chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: "Chancellor timber," Guo Wei said.

sentences.zh: 入城，訪求得之，甚喜。

translations.literal: After entering the city he sought Fan out and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the capital he found Fan Zhi and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 時大雪，威解所服紫袍衣之，令草太后誥令，迎新君儀注。

translations.literal: Snow was falling heavily; Guo Wei removed his own purple robe and clothed Fan in it, then had him draft the Empress Dowager's decree and the ceremonial protocol for welcoming the new sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow was falling. Guo Wei stripped off his own purple robe and put it on Fan, then had him draft the Empress Dowager's enthronement decree and the protocol for welcoming the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 蒼黃之中，討論撰定，皆得其宜。

translations.literal: In that rush and confusion, every point debated and fixed was judged apt.
translations.idiomatic: Amid the panic and haste, every clause they debated and settled proved sound.

sentences.zh: 初，隱帝遣供奉官押班陽曲張永德賜昭義節度使常思生辰物。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Hidden Emperor had sent Director of Attendants Zhang Yongde of Yangqu to deliver birthday gifts to Chang Si, Military Governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Hidden Emperor had sent Zhang Yongde of Yangqu, a director of palace attendants, to present birthday gifts to Chang Si, military governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 永德，郭威之婿也，會楊邠等誅，密詔思殺永德。

translations.literal: Yongde was Guo Wei's son-in-law; when Yang Bin and the others were executed, a secret edict ordered Chang Si to kill Yongde.
translations.idiomatic: Yongde was Guo Wei's son-in-law. When Yang Bin and his faction were killed, a secret order commanded Chang Si to murder him.

sentences.zh: 思素聞郭威多奇異，囚永德以觀變，及威克大梁，思乃釋永德而謝之。

translations.literal: Chang Si had long heard tales of Guo Wei's strangeness; he imprisoned Yongde to watch how events would turn, and when Guo Wei took Daliang, Chang released Yongde and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Si had long heard that Guo Wei was a man of uncanny fortune. He kept Yongde in custody to see which way the wind would blow; when Guo Wei seized Daliang, Chang freed Yongde and apologized.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，郭威帥百官上言：「比皇帝到闕，動涉浹旬，請太后臨朝聽政。」

translations.literal: On gengyin, Guo Wei led the officials in stating: "Before the Emperor reaches the capital it will take more than ten days—We ask the Empress Dowager to preside over court and hear affairs of government."
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Guo Wei led the officials in asking that the Empress Dowager preside over court, since the new emperor would not reach the capital for more than ten days."

sentences.zh: 先是，馬希萼遣蠻兵圍玉潭，朱進忠引兵會之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ma Xie had sent barbarian troops to besiege Yutan; Zhu Jinzhong led troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ma Xie had sent tribal warriors to besiege Yutan, and Zhu Jinzhong marched to join him.

sentences.zh: 崔洪璉兵敗，奔還長沙。

translations.literal: Cui Honglian's army was defeated and fled back to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Honglian was defeated and fled back to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 希萼引兵繼進，攻岳州，刺史王贇拒之，五日不克。

translations.literal: Xie pressed forward, attacked Yue Prefecture; Prefect Wang Yun resisted, and in five days Xie could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie pressed on to Yue Prefecture. Prefect Wang Yun held the city, and after five days Xie still could not take it.

sentences.zh: 希萼使人謂贇曰：「公非馬氏之臣乎？

translations.literal: Xie sent someone to tell Wang Yun: "Are you not a subject of the Ma house?
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie sent a messenger to Wang Yun: "Are you not a servant of the Ma house?

sentences.zh: 不事我，欲事異國乎？

translations.literal: If you will not serve me, do you mean to serve a foreign state?
translations.idiomatic: If you will not serve me, will you serve a foreign power instead?

sentences.zh: 為人臣而懷貳心，豈不辱其先人？」

translations.literal: To harbor divided loyalty as a subject—would that not disgrace your forebears?"
translations.idiomatic: A subject who keeps a second heart—would that not shame his ancestors?"

sentences.zh: 贇曰：「亡父為先王將，六破淮南兵。

translations.literal: Wang Yun said: "My late father served the late king as a general and six times broke the armies of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun answered, "My dead father served the late king as a general and six times routed the armies of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 今大王兄弟不相容，贇常恐淮南坐收其弊，一旦以遺體臣淮南，誠辱先人耳！

translations.literal: Now the great king's brothers cannot abide each other; I constantly fear Huainan will sit by and harvest our weakness—and that one day this mortal frame of mine should serve Huainan would truly disgrace my ancestors!
translations.idiomatic: Now the king's own brothers turn on each other. I live in fear that Huainan will sit back and profit from our ruin—and that one day this body of mine should bow to Huainan would be a true disgrace to my forebears!

sentences.zh: 大王苟能釋憾罷兵，兄弟雍睦如初，贇敢不盡死以事大王兄弟，豈有二心乎？」

translations.literal: If the great king can set aside resentment and cease hostilities, and the brothers live in harmony as before, dare I not give my life in serving the great king's brothers—would I have a second heart?"
translations.idiomatic: If you can lay down your grudge and sheathe your sword, and the brothers live in peace as before, I would gladly die in your service. Would I then keep a divided heart?"

sentences.zh: 希萼慚，引兵去。

translations.literal: Xie was ashamed and withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Ma Xie withdrew.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，至湘陰，焚掠而過。

translations.literal: On xinmao he reached Xiangyin, burning and plundering as he passed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao he reached Xiangyin and burned and looted his way through.

sentences.zh: 至長沙，軍於湘西，步兵及蠻兵軍於岳麓，朱進忠自玉潭引兵會之。

translations.literal: Reaching Changsha, he encamped west of the Xiang; infantry and barbarian troops encamped at Yuelu; Zhu Jinzhong led troops from Yutan to join him.
translations.idiomatic: At Changsha he camped west of the river; his foot soldiers and tribal auxiliaries camped at Yuelu, and Zhu Jinzhong brought his forces from Yutan to link up.

sentences.zh: 馬希廣遣劉彥瑫召水軍指揮使許可瓊帥戰艦五百艘屯城北津，屬於南津，以馬希崇為監軍。

translations.literal: Ma Xiguang sent Liu Yantang to summon Naval Commander Xu Keqiong to lead five hundred warships to station at the North Ford of the city, subordinate to the South Ford, with Ma Xichong as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiguang sent Liu Yantang to summon Xu Keqiong, commander of the river fleet, to anchor five hundred warships at the city's north ford under the south ford's command, with Ma Xichong as overseer.

sentences.zh: 又遣馬軍指揮使李彥溫將騎兵屯駝口，扼湘陰路，步軍指揮使韓禮將二千人屯楊柳橋，扼柵路。

translations.literal: He also sent Cavalry Commander Li Yanwen to lead horsemen to station at Tuokou, blocking the Xiangyin road; Infantry Commander Han Li to lead two thousand men to station at Yangliu Bridge, blocking the stockade road.
translations.idiomatic: He also posted Li Yanwen and his cavalry at Tuokou to block the road from Xiangyin, and Han Li with two thousand foot soldiers at Yangliu Bridge to block the stockade route.

sentences.zh: 可瓊，德勳之子也。

translations.literal: Keqiong was the son of Xu Dexun.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiong was the son of the famed general Xu Dexun.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，太后始臨朝，以王峻為樞密使，袁㠖為宣徽南院使，王殷為侍衛馬步軍都指揮使，郭崇威為侍衛馬軍都指揮使，曹威為侍衛步軍都指揮使，陳州刺史李穀權判三司。

translations.literal: On renchen the Empress Dowager began presiding over court; Wang Jun was made Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Yuan Yi, Commissioner of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat; Wang Yin, Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse and Foot; Guo Chongwei, Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Cavalry; Cao Wei, Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Infantry; Li Gu, Prefect of Chenzhou, was appointed acting head of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the Empress Dowager began to hold court. Wang Jun became director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Yuan Yi, commissioner of the southern palace secretariat; Wang Yin, commander of the palace guard horse and foot; Guo Chongwei, commander of palace cavalry; Cao Wei, commander of palace infantry; and Li Gu of Chenzhou was made acting head of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 劉銖、李洪建及其黨皆梟首於市，而赦其家。

translations.literal: Liu Zhu, Li Hongjian, and their faction were all displayed by decapitation in the marketplace, but their families were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhu, Li Hongjian, and their accomplices were beheaded and their heads displayed in the market, but their families were spared.

sentences.zh: 郭威謂公卿曰：「劉銖屠吾家，吾復屠其家，怨仇反覆，庸有極乎！」

translations.literal: Guo Wei told the high officials: "Liu Zhu slaughtered my household; if I slaughter his in turn, vengeance going back and forth—would it ever have an end?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei told the court, "Liu Zhu butchered my family. If I butcher his in turn, hatred will chase hatred forever—where would it end?"

sentences.zh: 由是數家獲免。

translations.literal: By this several households were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Several families were spared because of this.

sentences.zh: 王殷屢為洪建請免死，郭威不許。

translations.literal: Wang Yin repeatedly pleaded for Hongjian's life; Guo Wei would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin pleaded again and again for Hongjian's life, but Guo Wei refused.

sentences.zh: 後匡贊至兗州，慕容彥超執而獻之。

translations.literal: Later Kuang Zan reached Yanzhou; Murong Yanchao seized him and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hou Kuangzan fled to Yanzhou, where Murong Yanchao seized him and handed him over.

sentences.zh: 李業至陝州，其兄保義節度使洪信不敢匿於家。

translations.literal: Li Ye reached Shanzhou; his elder brother Hongxin, Military Governor of Baoyi, dared not hide him at home.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye reached Shanzhou, but his brother Hongxin, military governor of Baoyi, dared not shelter him.

sentences.zh: 業懷金將奔晉陽，至絳州，盜殺之而取其金。

translations.literal: Ye carried gold and was fleeing toward Jinyang; at Jiangzhou a robber killed him and took the gold.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye fled toward Jinyang with gold in his pack. At Jiangzhou a bandit killed him and stole it.

sentences.zh: 蜀施州刺史田行皋奔荊南。

translations.literal: Tian Xinggao, Prefect of Shi in Shu, fled to Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xinggao, prefect of Shi in Shu, defected to Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 高保融曰：「彼貳於蜀，安肯盡忠於我！」

translations.literal: Gao Baorong said: "He was disloyal to Shu—how would he serve us with whole-hearted loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baorong said, "A man who betrayed Shu will never serve us faithfully!"

sentences.zh: 執之，歸於蜀，伏誅。

translations.literal: He was seized, returned to Shu, and executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested, sent back to Shu, and executed.

sentences.zh: 鎮州、刑州奏：「契丹主將數萬騎入寇，攻內丘，五日不克，死傷其眾。

translations.literal: Zhenzhou and Xingzhou reported: "The Khitan ruler led tens of thousands of horsemen in invasion, attacked Neiqiu, and in five days could not take it; many of his men were killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: “Reports from Zhenzhou and Xingzhou said the Khitan khan had invaded with tens of thousands of horsemen, besieged Neiqiu for five days without success, and lost many men.

sentences.zh: 有戍兵五百叛應契丹，引契丹入城，屠之，又陷饒陽。」

translations.literal: Five hundred garrison soldiers rebelled and sided with the Khitan, leading them into the city; the city was massacred, and Raoyang also fell."
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred garrison troops mutinied, opened the gates to the Khitan, and the city was slaughtered. Raoyang fell next."

sentences.zh: 太后敕郭威將大軍擊之，國事權委竇貞固、蘇禹珪、王峻，軍事委王殷。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager ordered Guo Wei to lead the great army against them; state affairs were provisionally entrusted to Dou Zhengu, Su Yugui, and Wang Jun; military affairs to Wang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ordered Guo Wei north with the main army. Civil affairs were left to Dou Zhengu, Su Yugui, and Wang Jun; military affairs to Wang Yin.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲午朔，郭威發大梁。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the jiawu new moon, Guo Wei departed from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu new moon of the twelfth month, Guo Wei marched out of Daliang.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以翰林學士、戶部侍郎范質為樞密副使。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue Fan Zhi was made Deputy Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Fan Zhi, hanlin academician and vice minister of revenue, was appointed deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，蠻酋彭師暠降於楚，楚人惡其獷直。

translations.literal: Earlier, Pentou chieftain Peng Shigao had surrendered to Chu; the people of Chu disliked his blunt roughness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the tribal chief Peng Shigao had submitted to Chu, but the Chu court disliked his blunt, rough manner.

sentences.zh: 楚王希廣獨憐之，以為強弩指揮使，領辰州刺史，師暠常欲為希廣死。

translations.literal: King Xiguang alone took pity on him, appointing him Commander of Crossbows and making him Prefect of Chen; Shigao always wished to die for Xiguang.
translations.idiomatic: King Xiguang alone favored him, made him commander of crossbowmen and prefect of Chen, and Shigao was ready to die for him.

sentences.zh: 及朱進忠與蠻兵合七千餘人至長沙，營於江西，師暠登城望之，言於希廣曰：「朗人驟勝而驕，雜以蠻兵，攻之易破也。

translations.literal: When Zhu Jinzhong and the barbarian troops, more than seven thousand together, reached Changsha and encamped west of the river, Shigao mounted the wall to watch them and said to Xiguang: "The Lang men are suddenly victorious and arrogant, mixed with barbarian troops—strike them and they will break easily.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Jinzhong and more than seven thousand tribal soldiers reached Changsha and camped west of the river, Shigao climbed the wall to watch them and told Xiguang, "The Langzhou men are flush with a quick victory and drunk on pride, and their ranks are laced with tribesmen. Strike them and they will break.

sentences.zh: 願假臣步卒三千，自巴溪渡江，出岳麓之後，至水西，令許可瓊以戰艦渡江，腹背合擊，必破之。

translations.literal: I beg three thousand foot soldiers: I will cross the river at Baxi, come out behind Yuelu, reach the west bank of the water, and have Xu Keqiong ferry across with warships—we will strike front and rear together and surely break them.
translations.idiomatic: Give me three thousand foot soldiers. I will cross at Baxi, come out behind Yuelu, and take the west bank. Have Xu Keqiong ferry his warships across—we will crush them between hammer and anvil.

sentences.zh: 前軍敗，則其大軍自不敢輕進矣。」

translations.literal: If their vanguard is beaten, their main army will not dare advance lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Once their vanguard breaks, the main host will not dare press forward."

sentences.zh: 希廣將從之。

translations.literal: Xiguang was about to agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang was ready to assent.

sentences.zh: 時馬希萼已遣間使以厚利啖許可瓊，許分湖南而治，可瓊有貳心，乃謂希廣曰：「師暠與梅山諸蠻皆族類，安可信也！

translations.literal: By then Ma Xie had already sent secret emissaries with rich bribes to tempt Xu Keqiong, promising to divide Hunan and rule jointly; Keqiong had divided loyalties, and said to Xiguang: "Shigao and the Meishan barbarians are all of one tribe—how can he be trusted!
translations.idiomatic: By then Ma Xie had already bribed Xu Keqiong through secret agents, promising to split Hunan between them. Keqiong's heart was divided, and he told Xiguang, "Shigao and the Meishan tribes are kin—how can you trust him?

sentences.zh: 可瓊世為楚將，必不負大王，希萼竟何能為！」

translations.literal: I am a Chu general for generations—I could never fail the great king; what can Xie actually do!"
translations.idiomatic: My family has served Chu for generations. I would never betray you. What can Xie truly do?"

sentences.zh: 希廣乃止。

translations.literal: Xiguang then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 希萼尋以戰艦四百餘艘泊江西。

translations.literal: Xie soon anchored more than four hundred warships west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie soon moored more than four hundred warships on the west bank.

sentences.zh: 希廣命諸將皆受可瓊節度，日賜可瓊銀五百兩，希廣屢造其營計事。

translations.literal: Xiguang ordered all generals to accept Keqiong's command; each day he gave Keqiong five hundred taels of silver; Xiguang repeatedly visited his camp to plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang placed every general under Keqiong's command, sent him five hundred taels of silver each day, and visited his camp again and again to consult.

sentences.zh: 可瓊常閉壘，不使士卒知朗軍進退。

translations.literal: Keqiong often closed his ramparts and kept his soldiers ignorant of the Lang army's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiong kept his camp shut and hid from his men whether the Langzhou army advanced or retreated.

sentences.zh: 希廣歎曰：「真將軍也，吾何憂哉！」

translations.literal: Xiguang sighed: "A true general—I have nothing to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang sighed with relief: "A true general. What is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 可瓊或夜乘單舸詐稱巡江，與希萼會水西，約為內應。

translations.literal: Keqiong sometimes at night took a lone boat, falsely claiming to patrol the river, and met Xie west of the water, agreeing to act as insider.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiong would slip out at night in a single boat, pretending to patrol the river, and meet Ma Xie on the west bank to arrange treason from within.

sentences.zh: 一旦，彭師暠見可瓊，瞋目叱之，拂衣入見希廣曰：「可瓊將叛國，人皆知之，請速除之，無貽後患。」

translations.literal: One day Peng Shigao saw Keqiong, glared and rebuked him, then swept into see Xiguang: "Keqiong is about to betray the state—everyone knows it; please remove him at once, lest trouble follow."
translations.idiomatic: One day Shigao caught sight of Keqiong, glared at him, then strode in to Xiguang and said, "Keqiong is about to sell the kingdom—everyone knows it. Remove him now, before the wound festers."

sentences.zh: 希廣曰：「可瓊，許侍中之子，豈有是邪！」

translations.literal: Xiguang said: "Keqiong is the son of Attendant-in-Ordinary Xu—how could this be!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang replied, "Keqiong is the son of Xu Dexun. How could he do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 師暠退，歎曰：「王仁而不斷，敗亡可翹足俟也！」

translations.literal: Shigao withdrew and sighed: "The king is benevolent but cannot decide—ruin waits with lifted foot!"
translations.idiomatic: Shigao withdrew and sighed, "The king is kind but cannot choose. Disaster is only a step away."

sentences.zh: 潭州大雪，平地四尺，潭、朗兩軍久不得戰。

translations.literal: Heavy snow in Tanzhou—four feet on level ground; the Tan and Lang armies long could not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhou was buried in snow four feet deep on level ground, and the Tan and Lang armies could not come to blows for days.

sentences.zh: 希廣信巫覡及僧語，塑鬼於江上，舉手以卻朗兵，又作大像於高樓，手指水西，怒目視之，命眾僧日夜誦經，希廣自衣僧服膜拜求福。

translations.literal: Xiguang trusted shamans and monks: they molded a demon image on the river and raised a hand to repel the Lang troops; they also made a great statue on a high tower, finger pointing west across the water, glaring in anger, and ordered monks to chant day and night; Xiguang himself donned monastic robes and bowed in worship seeking fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang put his faith in shamans and monks. They molded a demon on the riverbank and lifted its hand to drive back the Langzhou army; they erected a giant idol on a tower, finger thrust toward the west bank, eyes blazing, and set monks to chant without rest. Xiguang himself put on monk's robes and bowed for luck.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，朗州步軍指揮使武陵何敬真等以蠻兵三千陳於楊柳橋，敬真望韓禮營旌旗紛錯，曰：「彼眾已懼，擊之易破也。」

translations.literal: On jiachen, Lang Prefecture Infantry Commander He Jingzhen of Wuling and others deployed three thousand barbarian troops at Yangliu Bridge; Jingzhen looked at Han Li's camp with banners in disorder and said: "Their masses are already afraid—strike and they will break easily."
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, He Jingzhen of Wuling and other Langzhou infantry commanders drew up three thousand tribal soldiers at Yangliu Bridge. Jingzhen saw Han Li's banners in confusion and said, "They are already rattled. Hit them and they will shatter."

sentences.zh: 朗人雷暉衣潭卒之服潛入禮寨，手劍擊禮，不中，軍中驚擾。

translations.literal: A Lang man, Lei Hui, dressed in Tan soldiers' garb slipped into Li's camp, sword in hand, and struck at Li—he missed, and the army was thrown into alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Hui, a Langzhou man disguised in Tan uniform, stole into Han Li's camp and lunged at him with a sword. He missed, but the camp erupted in panic.

sentences.zh: 敬真等乘其亂擊之，禮軍大潰，禮被創走，至家而卒。

translations.literal: Jingzhen and the others struck amid the chaos; Li's army broke completely; Li was wounded and fled, dying at home.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen charged into the confusion. Han Li's force collapsed. Li was wounded, fled home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 於是朗兵水陸急攻長沙，步軍指揮使吳宏、小門使楊滌相謂曰：「以死報國，此其時矣！」

translations.literal: Then the Lang army pressed Changsha by land and water; Infantry Commander Wu Hong and Junior Gate Commissioner Yang Di said to each other: "To repay the state with death—this is the hour!"
translations.idiomatic: The Langzhou army then pressed Changsha by land and water. Infantry commander Wu Hong and junior gate commissioner Yang Di said to each other, "If not now, when do we repay the state with our lives?"

sentences.zh: 各引兵出戰。

translations.literal: Each led troops out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Each marched out to fight.

sentences.zh: 宏出清泰門，戰不利。

translations.literal: Hong went out the Gate of Pure Felicity; the battle went badly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hong sallied from the Gate of Pure Felicity and was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 滌出長樂，戰自辰至午，朗兵小卻。

translations.literal: Di went out from Changle; they fought from chen hour to wu hour, and the Lang troops gave ground slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Di went out from Changle and fought from morning until noon, forcing the Langzhou lines back a little.

sentences.zh: 許可瓊、劉彥瑫按兵不救。

translations.literal: Xu Keqiong and Liu Yantang held their troops and did not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Keqiong and Liu Yantang held their men back and did not move to help.

sentences.zh: 滌士卒饑疲，退就食。

translations.literal: Di's soldiers, hungry and weary, withdrew to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Di's exhausted, hungry soldiers fell back to eat.

sentences.zh: 彭師暠戰於城東北隅。

translations.literal: Peng Shigao fought at the northeast corner of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shigao fought at the northeast corner of the wall.

sentences.zh: 蠻兵自城東縱火，城上人招許可瓊軍使救城，可瓊舉全軍降希萼，長沙遂陷。

translations.literal: Barbarian troops set fire from the east of the city; men on the wall beckoned Xu Keqiong's army to save the city; Keqiong surrendered his entire force to Xie, and Changsha fell.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal soldiers torched the eastern quarter. Defenders on the wall cried to Xu Keqiong's fleet for help. Instead Keqiong surrendered his whole force to Ma Xie, and Changsha fell.

sentences.zh: 朗兵及蠻兵大掠三日，殺吏民，焚廬舍，自武穆王以來所營宮室，皆為灰燼，所積寶貨，皆入蠻落。

translations.literal: Lang and barbarian troops looted for three days, killing officials and people, burning dwellings; palaces built since King Wumu were all ash; accumulated treasures all went into barbarian hands.
translations.idiomatic: Lang and tribal soldiers looted for three days, killing officials and common people and burning houses. Every palace raised since King Wumu was reduced to ash, and the hoarded wealth vanished into the hill country.

sentences.zh: 李彥溫望見城中火起，自駝口引兵救之，朗人已據城拒戰。

translations.literal: Li Yanwen saw fire rise in the city from Tuokou and led troops to rescue; the Lang men already held the city and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: From Tuokou, Li Yanwen saw flames over the city and rushed to relieve it, but the Langzhou men already held the walls and fought him off.

sentences.zh: 彥溫攻清泰門，不克，與劉彥瑫各將千餘人奉文昭王及希廣諸子趣袁州，遂奔唐。

translations.literal: Yanwen attacked the Gate of Pure Felicity without success; he and Liu Yantang each led more than a thousand men escorting King Wenzhao and Xiguang's sons toward Yuanzhou, then fled to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwen assaulted the Gate of Pure Felicity and failed. He and Liu Yantang each took more than a thousand men, escorted King Wenzhao and Xiguang's sons toward Yuanzhou, and fled to Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 張暉降於希萼。

translations.literal: Zhang Hui surrendered to Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hui submitted to Ma Xie.

sentences.zh: 左司馬希崇帥將吏詣希萼勸進。

translations.literal: Left Marshal Xichong led officers to Xie urging him to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Left marshal Ma Xichong led the officers to Ma Xie and urged him to take power.

sentences.zh: 吳宏戰，血滿袖，見希萼曰：「不幸為許可瓊所誤，今日死，不愧先王矣！」

translations.literal: Wu Hong, blood soaking his sleeves, faced Xie and said: "Unluckily misled by Xu Keqiong—dying today, I am not ashamed before the late king!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Hong, his sleeves drenched in blood, faced Ma Xie and said, "Xu Keqiong misled us. If I die today, I will not shame the late king."

sentences.zh: 彭師暠投槊於地，大呼請死。

translations.literal: Peng Shigao cast his spear to the ground and cried out asking for death.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shigao threw down his spear and shouted that he wished to die.

sentences.zh: 希萼歎曰：「鐵石人也！」

translations.literal: Xie sighed: "Men of iron and stone!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie sighed, "Men cast from iron and stone."

sentences.zh: 皆不殺。

translations.literal: He killed none of them.
translations.idiomatic: He spared them both.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，希崇迎希萼入府視事，閉城，分捕希廣及掌書記李弘皋、弟弘節、都軍判官唐昭胤及鄧懿文、楊滌等，皆獲之。

translations.literal: On yisi, Xichong welcomed Xie into the headquarters to preside, closed the city, and sent parties to capture Xiguang, Chief Secretary Li Honggao, his brother Hongjie, Army Judge Tang Zhaoyin, Deng Yiwen, Yang Di, and others—all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Xichong ushered Ma Xie into the prefectural seat to take command, sealed the city, and sent parties to seize Xiguang, chief secretary Li Honggao, his brother Hongjie, army judge Tang Zhaoyin, Deng Yiwen, Yang Di, and others. All were captured.

sentences.zh: 希萼謂希廣曰：「承父兄之業，豈無長幼乎？」

translations.literal: Xie said to Xiguang: "In inheriting father and elder brother's enterprise—is there no order of senior and junior?"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie said to Xiguang, "When a man inherits his father's and elder brother's realm, does he not know elder from younger?"

sentences.zh: 希廣曰：「將吏見推，朝廷見命耳。」

translations.literal: Xiguang said: "The officers pushed me forward; the court appointed me—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Xiguang answered, "The officers chose me, and the court confirmed it—that is all."

sentences.zh: 希萼皆囚之。

translations.literal: Xie imprisoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie had them all imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 丙午，希萼命內外巡檢侍衛指揮使劉賓禁止焚掠。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Xie ordered Inner and Outer Patrol Commander Liu Bin to forbid burning and looting.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Ma Xie ordered patrol commander Liu Bin to stop the burning and looting.

sentences.zh: 丁未，希萼自稱天策上將軍、武安、武平、靜江、寧遠等軍節度使、楚王。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Xie styled himself Generalissimo of the Heavenly Strategy, Military Governor of the Wuan, Wuping, Jingjiang, Ningyuan, and other circuits, King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Ma Xie proclaimed himself generalissimo of the Heavenly Strategy, military governor of Wuan, Wuping, Jingjiang, Ningyuan, and other circuits, and king of Chu.

sentences.zh: 以希崇為節度副使、判官府事，湖南要職，悉以朗人為之。

translations.literal: He made Xichong Deputy Military Governor and administrator of headquarters affairs; all key posts in Hunan he filled with Lang men.
translations.idiomatic: He made Xichong deputy military governor and head of headquarters affairs, and filled every important post in Hunan with men from Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 臠食李弘皋、弘節、唐昭胤、楊滌，斬鄧懿文於市。

translations.literal: He cut apart Li Honggao, Hongjie, Tang Zhaoyin, and Yang Di; Deng Yiwen was beheaded in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: He had Li Honggao, Hongjie, Tang Zhaoyin, and Yang Di cut to pieces and ate their flesh; Deng Yiwen was beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 戊申，希萼謂將吏曰：「希廣懦夫，為左右所制耳，吾欲生之，可乎？」

translations.literal: On wushen, Xie said to officers: "Xiguang is a weakling, controlled by those around him—I wish to let him live; may I?"
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Ma Xie asked his officers, "Xiguang is a coward pushed around by his counselors. I want to let him live. May I?"

sentences.zh: 諸將皆不對。

translations.literal: The officers all kept silent.
translations.idiomatic: The officers said nothing.

sentences.zh: 朱進忠嘗為希廣所答，對曰：「大王三年血戰，始得長沙，一國不容二主，他日必悔之。」

translations.literal: Zhu Jinzhong had once been flogged by Xiguang and answered: "Great king, you fought in blood for three years before you took Changsha—a state cannot hold two masters; one day you will regret sparing him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jinzhong, whom Xiguang had once beaten, answered, "Great king, you bled for three years to win Changsha. A kingdom cannot hold two rulers. One day you will regret mercy."

sentences.zh: 戊申，賜希廣死。

translations.literal: On wushen, Xiguang was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Xiguang was put to death.

sentences.zh: 希廣臨刑，猶誦佛書，彭師暠葬之於瀏陽門外。

translations.literal: Facing execution, Xiguang still recited Buddhist scriptures; Peng Shigao buried him outside the Liuyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the block Xiguang still recited sutras. Peng Shigao buried him outside the Liuyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使贇留右都押牙鞏延美、元從都教練使楊溫守徐州，與馮道等西來，在道仗衛，皆如王者，左右呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Military Governor of Wuning Yun left Right Chief Guard Geng Yanmei and Original Followers Training Commander Yang Wen to hold Xuzhou; traveling west with Feng Dao and others, on the road his escort and guards were all as for a king; attendants cried "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun, military governor of Wuning, left Geng Yanmei and Yang Wen to hold Xuzhou and marched west with Feng Dao and the others. On the road his escort matched a sovereign's, and his attendants shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 郭威至滑州。

translations.literal: Guo Wei reached Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei reached Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 留數日，贇遣使慰勞。

translations.literal: After several days' stay, Yun sent envoys to offer comfort and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: After several days there, Yun sent envoys to comfort and reward the army.

sentences.zh: 諸將受命之際，相顧不拜，私相謂曰：「我輩屠陷京城，其罪大矣，若劉氏復立，我輩尚有種乎！」

translations.literal: When the generals received their orders they looked at each other and did not bow; privately they said: "We sacked and ruined the capital—our crime is great; if the Liu house is restored, will any seed of us remain!"
translations.idiomatic: When the generals received Yun's orders they looked at one another and refused to bow. Among themselves they said, "We plundered the capital. Our crime is grave. If the Liu house returns, will any of us survive?"

sentences.zh: 己酉，威聞之，即引兵行，趣澶州。

translations.literal: On jiyou, when Guo Wei heard this he immediately marched, heading for Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, hearing this, Guo Wei marched at once for Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，遣蘇禹珪如宋州迎嗣君。

translations.literal: On xinhai, he sent Su Yugui to Songzhou to welcome the heir.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he sent Su Yugui to Songzhou to welcome the heir.

sentences.zh: 楚王希萼以子光贊為武平留後，以何敬真為朗州牙內都指揮使，將兵戍之。

translations.literal: King Xie appointed his son Guangzan Military Commissioner of Wuping; He Jingzhen as Langzhou Internal Guard Commander, garrisoning with troops.
translations.idiomatic: King Ma Xie made his son Guangzan military commissioner of Wuping and appointed He Jingzhen commander of Langzhou's inner guard to garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 希萼召拓跋恆，欲用之，恆稱疾不起。

translations.literal: Xie summoned Tuoba Heng intending to employ him; Heng claimed illness and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xie summoned Tuoba Heng to office, but Heng pleaded illness and would not serve.

sentences.zh: 壬子，郭威渡河，館於澶州。

translations.literal: On renzi, Guo Wei crossed the river and lodged at Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Guo Wei crossed the Yellow River and lodged at Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑旦，將發，將士數千人忽大噪。

translations.literal: At dawn on guichou, as he was about to depart, several thousand officers and soldiers suddenly raised a great uproar.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on guichou, just as he was about to march, several thousand soldiers broke into a roar.

sentences.zh: 威命閉門，將士逾垣登屋而入曰：「天子須侍中自為之，將士已與劉氏為仇，不可立也！」

translations.literal: Guo Wei ordered the gates closed; soldiers climbed walls and roofs to enter, saying: "The Son of Heaven must be the Attendant-in-Ordinary himself—the troops are already enemies of the Liu house; he cannot be enthroned!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei ordered the gates shut, but soldiers scaled the walls and roofs and burst in, shouting, "The throne must go to the Attendant-in-Ordinary himself! We are already enemies of the Liu house—Yun cannot be emperor!"

sentences.zh: 或裂黃旗以被威體，共扶抱之，呼萬歲震地，因擁威南行。

translations.literal: Some tore yellow banners to drape Guo Wei's body; they supported and embraced him, cries of "Ten thousand years!" shaking the earth, and bore Guo Wei southward.
translations.idiomatic: Some ripped yellow banners and draped them over Guo Wei. They lifted him up, crying "Long live the emperor!" until the ground shook, and carried him south.

sentences.zh: 威乃上太后箋，請奉漢宗廟，事太后為母。

translations.literal: Guo Wei then submitted a memorial to the Empress Dowager asking to uphold the Han ancestral temple and serve the Empress Dowager as his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei then memorialized the Empress Dowager, pledging to preserve the Han ancestral temples and honor her as his mother.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，至韋城，下書撫諭大梁士民，以昨離河上，在道秋毫不犯，勿有懷疑。

translations.literal: On bingchen, reaching Weicheng, he issued a letter reassuring the people of Daliang that since leaving the Yellow River yesterday not a hair had been harmed on the road—they should not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, at Weicheng, he issued a proclamation to calm the people of Daliang: since he had left the river the day before, not a blade of grass had been touched on the march—they need not fear.

sentences.zh: 戊午，威至七里店，竇貞固帥百官出迎拜謁，因勸進。

translations.literal: On wuwu, reaching Qili Store, Dou Zhengu led officials out to welcome and bow, then urged him to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, at Qili Store, Dou Zhengu led the officials out to welcome him and urged him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 威營於皋門村。

translations.literal: Guo Wei encamped at Gaomen Village.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei camped at Gaomen Village.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使贇已至宋州，王峻、王殷聞澶州軍變，遣侍衛馬軍都指揮使郭崇威將七百騎往拒之，又遣前申州刺史馬鐸將兵詣許州巡檢。

translations.literal: Military Governor Yun had already reached Songzhou; Wang Jun and Wang Yin, hearing of the mutiny at Danzhou, sent Palace Guard Cavalry Commander Guo Chongwei with seven hundred horsemen to block him, and also sent former Prefect of Shenzhou Ma Duo with troops to Xuzhou for inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun had already reached Songzhou. When Wang Jun and Wang Yin heard of the mutiny at Danzhou, they sent Guo Chongwei with seven hundred cavalry to intercept him and Ma Duo, former prefect of Shenzhou, to Xuzhou on patrol.

sentences.zh: 崇威忽至宋州，陳於府門外，贇大驚，闔門登樓詰之。

translations.literal: Chongwei suddenly arrived at Songzhou and formed up outside the headquarters gate; Yun was greatly alarmed, shut the gates, mounted the tower, and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei suddenly appeared at Songzhou and drew up his men outside the prefectural gate. Yun was terrified, barred the doors, climbed the tower, and demanded an explanation.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「澶州軍變，郭公慮陛下未察，故遣崇威來宿衛，無他也。」

translations.literal: He answered: "There was a mutiny at Danzhou; Lord Guo feared Your Majesty had not grasped it, so he sent Chongwei to guard you overnight—nothing more."
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei answered, "There was a mutiny at Danzhou. Lord Guo feared you had not understood the danger, so he sent me to guard you through the night—nothing more."

sentences.zh: 贇召崇威，崇威不敢進。

translations.literal: Yun summoned Chongwei; Chongwei dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Yun summoned Chongwei inside, but Chongwei would not enter.

sentences.zh: 馮道出與崇威語，崇威乃登樓，贇執崇威手而泣。

translations.literal: Feng Dao went out to speak with Chongwei; only then did Chongwei ascend the tower; Yun took Chongwei's hand and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao went out to parley with him, and only then did Chongwei climb the tower. Yun took his hand and wept.

sentences.zh: 崇威以郭威意安諭之。

translations.literal: Chongwei reassured him with Guo Wei's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei soothed him with Guo Wei's assurances.

sentences.zh: 少頃，崇威出，時護聖指揮使張令超帥部兵為贇宿衛，徐州判官董裔說贇曰：「觀崇威視瞻舉措，必有異謀。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Chongwei went out; at the time Guardian Sage Commander Zhang Lingchao led his troops guarding Yun overnight; Xuzhou Judge Dong Yi advised Yun: "Watching Chongwei's glances and movements, he surely harbors some other design.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chongwei left. Zhang Lingchao of the Guardian Sage command was then guarding Yun with his troops. Dong Yi, judge of Xuzhou, warned Yun, "Look at Chongwei's eyes and bearing—he is plotting something.

sentences.zh: 道路皆言郭威已為帝，而陛下深入不止，禍其至哉！

translations.literal: Every road says Guo Wei is already emperor, yet Your Majesty presses deeper without stopping—disaster must be near!
translations.idiomatic: Every road says Guo Wei is already emperor, yet you keep marching west. Ruin is close!

sentences.zh: 請急召張令超，諭以禍福，使夜以兵動崇威，奪其兵。

translations.literal: Summon Zhang Lingchao urgently, explain fortune and ruin, and have him by night move troops against Chongwei and seize his force.
translations.idiomatic: Summon Zhang Lingchao at once, show him what is at stake, and have him strike Chongwei by night and take his troops.

sentences.zh: 明日，掠睢陽金帛，募士卒，北走晉陽。

translations.literal: Tomorrow, plunder Suīyang's gold and silk, recruit soldiers, and flee north to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow seize the gold and silk of Suiyang, raise soldiers, and flee north to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 彼新定京邑，未暇追我，此策之上也！」

translations.literal: They have just settled the capital and will not have leisure to pursue—this is the best stratagem!"
translations.idiomatic: They have only just taken the capital and will not have time to chase you. It is the best plan left."

sentences.zh: 贇猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Yun hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yun wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 是夕，崇威密誘令超，令超帥眾歸之。

translations.literal: That evening Chongwei secretly won over Lingchao; Lingchao led his masses to join him.
translations.idiomatic: That night Chongwei secretly turned Zhang Lingchao, and Lingchao brought his men over to him.

sentences.zh: 贇大懼。

translations.literal: Yun was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 郭威遺贇書，雲為諸軍所迫，召馮道先歸，留趙上交、王度奉侍。

translations.literal: Guo Wei sent Yun a letter saying he was forced by the armies; he recalled Feng Dao first, leaving Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei wrote to Yun that the army had forced his hand. He recalled Feng Dao first and left Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to attend him.

sentences.zh: 道辭行，贇曰：「寡人此來所恃者，以公三十年舊相，故無疑耳。

translations.literal: As Feng Dao took leave, Yun said: "In coming here I relied on you—a minister of thirty years—so I had no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Dao prepared to leave, Yun said, "I came west trusting you—a minister of thirty years—so I had no fear.

sentences.zh: 今崇威奪吾衛兵，事危矣，公何以為計？」

translations.literal: Now Chongwei has taken my guard troops; affairs are perilous—what plan do you advise?"
translations.idiomatic: Now Chongwei has stripped me of my guard. The danger is real. What do you advise?"

sentences.zh: 道默然。

translations.literal: Feng Dao was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said nothing.

sentences.zh: 客將賈貞數目道，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Client officer Jia Zhen repeatedly signaled at Feng Dao, wanting to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhen, a client officer, kept catching Feng Dao's eye as if to urge his murder.

sentences.zh: 贇曰：「汝輩勿草草，此無預馮公事。」

translations.literal: Yun said: "You must not act rashly—this has nothing to do with Master Feng."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "Do nothing rash. This is not Master Feng's fault."

sentences.zh: 崇威遷贇於外館，殺其腹心董裔、賈貞等數人。

translations.literal: Chongwei moved Yun to an outer lodge and killed his trusted men Dong Yi, Jia Zhen, and several others.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwei moved Yun to a guest house and killed his confidants Dong Yi, Jia Zhen, and several others.

sentences.zh: 己未，太后誥，廢贇為湘陰公。

translations.literal: On jiwei, the Empress Dowager decreed deposing Yun as Duke of Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the Empress Dowager deposed Yun and made him Duke of Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 馬鐸引兵入許州，劉信惶惑自殺。

translations.literal: Ma Duo led troops into Xuzhou; Liu Xin, distraught, killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Duo marched into Xuzhou. Liu Xin, in panic, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 庚申，太后誥，以侍中監國。

translations.literal: On gengshen, the Empress Dowager decreed the Attendant-in-Ordinary as regent.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, the Empress Dowager named the Attendant-in-Ordinary regent of the realm.

sentences.zh: 百官籓鎮相繼上表勸進。

translations.literal: Officials and military governors one after another submitted memorials urging ascension.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and frontier governors one after another submitted memorials urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 壬戌夜，監國營有步兵將校醉，揚言向者澶州騎兵扶立，今步兵亦欲扶立，監國斬之。

translations.literal: On the night of renxu, a drunken infantry officer in the regent's camp publicly declared that just as the Danzhou cavalry had forced the enthronement, now the infantry wanted to force it too—the regent executed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of renxu, a drunken infantry officer in the regent's camp shouted that if the Danzhou cavalry could force an emperor onto the throne, the foot soldiers could do the same. The regent had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 南漢主以宮人盧瓊仙、黃瓊芝為女侍中，朝服冠帶，參決政事。

translations.literal: The ruler of Southern Han made palace women Lu Qiongxian and Huang Qiongzhi Female Attendants-in-Ordinary—they wore court dress, caps, and belts and took part in deciding government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Southern Han made the palace women Lu Qiongxian and Huang Qiongzhi female attendants-in-ordinary. They wore court robes, caps, and belts and joined in deciding state affairs.

sentences.zh: 宗室勳舊，誅戮殆盡，惟宦官林延遇等用事。

translations.literal: Members of the imperial clan and meritorious elders were slaughtered almost to extinction; only eunuchs such as Lin Yanyu held power.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clan and old meritocrats had been slaughtered almost to the last man; only eunuchs such as Lin Yanyu ran the court.
